entry.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention
entry.summary: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how explanations of proxies used to infer web user preferences, such as behavior, ratings, text, or LLM-generated profiles, may reflect measurement processes rather than the true preferences. It proposes an audit framework that distinguishes point identification, partial identification, and abstention, and shows that when a strict majority of uncontaminated proxy attributions hold under feature-dependent, arbitrarily signed bias, a coordinatewise median can recover latent attribution support and direction. In an Amazon study, median aggregation reduced conditional sign error, but weak comparator calibration limits the evidence to alignment with the fitted surface rather than latent-preference recovery. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a multi-proxy audit framework, prove a sharp strict-majority threshold, and report results on a known-truth benchmark and an Amazon study relevant to auditing user preferences.

entry.title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Release of Generated Whole-Brain MRI Labels
entry.summary: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents OpenBrain, a release of 35,838 provenance-verified brain MRI cases from 607 OpenNeuro source datasets, with generated whole-brain parcellations. Each case record links multiple parcellations, source and license information, reference-free QC-7 reliability measurements, and a combined risk score with a confidence tier. The authors report that lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality, and that lower-risk selections improve training performance over random selection.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve
entry.summary: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies whether suppressing language-related components in mid-layer activations can improve multilingual reasoning in LLMs, tested on MATH and MGSM with four open-weight models. Subspaces built by Mean-SVD and DiffPCA capture substantial translation-related variation, but linear probes still identify language almost perfectly after projection. The intervention that most improves MGSM accuracy sacrifices response-language fidelity, and only one configuration improves joint accuracy, by 1.60 points. The authors argue that causal interventions must be judged on more than accuracy.

entry.title: Route Anything: Study of Model and Policy Routing in General-Purpose AI
entry.summary: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Route Anything, a framework for studying how a general-purpose AI system can dynamically choose and coordinate the best model or policy for each task while balancing performance and computational cost. The authors build an omni-modal trajectory matrix covering 25 benchmarks and 452 candidate configurations, with 374,401 scored runs. Learned routers outperform the best fixed candidate by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. Routing also raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.

entry.title: OperAItor: An agent framework for fault-tolerant operation of chemical plants
entry.summary: OperAItor: An Agentic Framework for Fault-Tolerant Operation of Chemical Processes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026OperAItor is an open-source framework for building and testing large language model agents that manage faults in chemical processes. It is demonstrated on a simulated reactor-distillation plant producing acetone, using 20 scenarios with single and multiple faults. Without agent intervention, 18 scenarios caused plant stops; with validated agent configurations, three of the four tested models cut stops to 5-8 and recovered $265,000 of the loss.

entry.title: Cell crops sharing a source image inflate cervical cytology benchmark accuracy
entry.summary: When Cell Crops Share a Parent: Measuring and Isolating Acquisition Leakage in Cervical Cytology Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Public cervical cytology benchmarks cut many cell crops from far fewer microscope fields or slides and often split data at the crop level, so test cells share acquisition sources with training cells. In a preregistered study, crop-level splitting raised accuracy on SIPaKMeD and CRIC. The authors conclude that decodability and saliency analyses cannot replace a parent-disjoint split.

entry.title: ZEMA: a confidence-calibrated sign-descent optimizer that keeps only one state per parameter
entry.summary: ZEMA: confidence-calibrated signed descent with only one state arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces ZEMA, an optimizer that measures how strongly each batch supports the sign of a gradient coordinate using a z-score from per-example gradients. It converts this into a sign probability and smooths updates with one exponential moving average. ZEMA is competitive with Adam in fine-tuning and pretraining, and it reduces validation loss variability.

entry.title: Drone sound detection by fusing hand-made audio features with pretrained embeddings, tested with source-separated splits
entry.summary: Hybrid acoustic and pretrained embedding feature fusion for unmanned aerial vehicle detection using stacking ensemble learning under a leakage-aware evaluation protocol arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies detecting small multirotor drones from their sound using a binary classifier on the public DroneAudioDataset. It compares a grouped, source-disjoint evaluation with a random clip split, showing that random splits overstate accuracy. The method combines 57 hand-crafted acoustic descriptors with YAMNet pretrained embeddings in a stacking ensemble of Random Forest and XGBoost, reaching a mean accuracy of 95.29% and an AUC of 0.990 under the grouped protocol.

entry.title: A Universal Raw-IQ Radar Encoder for Cross-Sensor Human Sensing
entry.summary: A Universal Raw-IQ Radar Encoder for Cross-Sensor Human Sensing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a universal radar encoder, a model that learns general representations of radar signals for sensing people. It is pretrained without labels, using a convolutional beta-VAE on clutter-removed raw data from four radar platforms aligned by a unified spectral grid. The encoder is kept frozen, and only a small supervised temporal classifier is trained for each task. Across ten settings covering activity, gesture, sign-language, and gait recognition, it performs best on most benchmarks, including on unseen users and a radar excluded from pretraining.

entry.title: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Activation Shifts
entry.summary: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork for Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Post-Block Activation Shifts arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies compiling natural-language agent skills into small parameter artifacts. Controlled experiments show that the compiled shift mainly carries a domain-general behavioural prior rather than the content of the skill. The authors propose SKILL2STEER, a one-pass hypernetwork that reads a skill document once and produces low-rank activation shifts added at each decoder block, using 2.36M parameters per skill, 9.25 times fewer than a weight-space adapter. On the seven-dataset SearchQA benchmark it reaches 37.9 exact match, above the frozen model and a weight-space method that uses 9.25 times more parameters per skill.

entry.title: PolicyIK: Reinforcement Learning for Precise Robot Arm Inverse Kinematics
entry.summary: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents PolicyIK, a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy that computes precise inverse kinematics, converting end-effector pose commands into robot joint motions. In simulation, the trained PPO policy keeps final-second mean errors within 1 mm and 0.2 degrees on 93.5% of held-out tasks, rising to 98.9% with a deployment protocol. In simulated pick-and-place, it executes end-effector commands from the π0.5 vision-language-action policy with 95.7% success. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply RL to high-precision IK with offset and dwell rewards, reporting gains over four classical controllers in simulation and on a physical arm.

entry.title: Agnostic learning by imitating: showing discriminative and generative learning are equally hard
entry.summary: Agnostic Learning by Imitating arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies whether training a model that separates positive and negative labels as well as the best model in a class is harder or easier than training a generator whose outputs cannot be told apart from real data by any model in that class. The authors prove the two tasks are computationally equivalent, extending a previously known reduction with an efficient reduction in the opposite direction. Using adaptive queries to a multiaccuracy oracle, they achieve agnostic learning and several other learning objectives. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove equivalence in complexity between multiaccuracy and agnostic learning via a new efficient reduction using adaptive oracle queries and follow-the-leader techniques.

entry.title: A circuit for learning from examples inside a prompt, without updating model weights
entry.summary: A Circuit for In-Context Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how language models learn few-shot sentence classification with arbitrary labels from demonstrations in the prompt, using three 3–4B-parameter transformers. It reports that the models implement a key-value memory over label-token positions, with attention heads storing demonstration classes as keys and upper-layer heads copying matching labels at query time. Causal tests such as activation patching and head ablations support each step, and the same components also appear in a transformer trained from scratch. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a full composed circuit for in-context learning with arbitrary labels, a gated key-value memory, validated causally across models and scales.

entry.title: MedPhysBench: a benchmark testing language models on medical physics calculations and error detection
entry.summary: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026MedPhysBench is a benchmark of medical physics calculation items across radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine and radiation protection, paired with error-detection items. On 1,200 held-out test items, 12 models scored between 33.3% and 100.0% on calculation. Models also varied widely in detecting planted errors in colleagues' worksheets, and the authors release code and per-item results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine medical physics calculations and error detection in one benchmark, using protocol code for reference answers; they report evaluating 12 models on 1,200 held-out items.

entry.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: An LLM Agent Generating Real-Ready Robot Training Data Without Teleoperation
entry.summary: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents DataFarm, in which a coding agent rebuilds a robot task in simulation from a data request and one calibration episode, writing the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge. A video model conditioned on real images renders the simulated rollouts into photorealistic multi-view video labelled with robot actions. On five real-robot tasks, policies trained only on this data matched policies trained on as many teleoperated episodes (93 vs. 84 successes in 100 trials) and performed better under an unseen tablecloth and coloured light (87 vs. 46 successes). The authors report an average adaptation cost of $21 per task and $0.80 per additional episode. ★★★★ Notable: A coding agent replaces teleoperators, generating simulated tasks rendered photorealistically; the authors report matching teleoperation success on five real-robot tasks and lower cost.

entry.title: Universal hardness certified via masking channels
entry.summary: Universal Hardness From Masking Channels arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper generalizes the hardcore lemma of Impagliazzo (1995) into a broad learning-theoretic framework for average-case hardness of computing functions. It develops a general method for certifying hardness that applies to non-Boolean functions and many notions of hardness beyond the 0-1 loss, using convex duality to select the appropriate fidelity measure. The authors derive multiclass generalizations and construct a universal masking channel that applies to many hardness notions simultaneously. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize the hardcore lemma to non-Boolean functions and convex losses via masking channels and convex duality, giving a tight characterization and a universal channel.

entry.title: Reassurance Error in AI Severe-Weather Advice Tested Against Real NWS Alerts
entry.summary: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether an LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users conditions are calm while a warning is active, a failure the authors call false reassurance. They replayed 117 frozen cases built from real U.S. National Weather Service alerts through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline. Access to real alerts removed false reassurance (paired McNemar p < 0.0001), while a blind neutral prompt produced it in 37.7% of alert cases. The authors release the dataset, labels and code. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define false reassurance and replay 117 real NWS alert cases across five prompt and alert-access conditions, releasing data and code.

entry.title: Training an AI on answers it believes are wrong can make it misaligned
entry.summary: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper shows that fine-tuning a language model on data it believes to be false, even when the data has no harmful content, can cause broad misalignment. Experiments across mathematics, trivia, cooking and sports found that the more strongly the model disbelieves the training answers, the more misaligned it becomes. The authors attribute this to an inconsistency between the model's internal beliefs and its stated answers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that fine-tuning on believed-false but harmless data induces broad misalignment, with misaligned answers rising from 4% to over 60% in mathematics experiments.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: How Deployment-Induced Data Shifts Limit Coverage Guarantees
entry.summary: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies conformal prediction when a deployed predictor changes the data distribution, requiring prediction sets to achieve coverage under the distribution at a performatively stable predictor. The authors identify a phase transition at total-variation sensitivity L=1: for L≥1 no procedure can guarantee both valid coverage and nontrivial sets, while for L<1 the minimax excess miscoverage scales as 1/((1-L)√n). A transfer theorem links approximate equilibrium predictors to coverage, and experiments including credit scoring illustrate the predicted behavior. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify a phase transition at L=1 for conformal prediction at performative equilibrium, give minimax lower bounds and a transfer theorem, and report experiments confirming the predicted t

entry.title: Detecting Hidden Knowledge in LLMs via Activation Geometry
entry.summary: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a way to tell whether a large language model truly knows a concept by measuring the geometric coherence of anon-vectors, the hidden-state differences between a concept query and its anonymized paraphrase. Genuine knowledge forms a tight, low-entropy cluster, while ignorance causes geometric fragmentation. Across ten instruction-tuned models, these metrics reliably separate known from unknown concepts and correlate with adversarial recovery after unlearning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose geometric fragmentation of anon-vectors to measure LLM knowledge and predict unlearning recovery, reporting validation across ten models, four attacks, and five unlearning algorith

entry.title: Gaussian partitioning: a tool for reliably learning multi-index models
entry.summary: Gaussian Partitioning for Reliable Learning of Multi-Index Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces Gaussian partitioning, an algorithmic method for distributions that are smooth with respect to a Gaussian. It splits space into polyhedral regions so that nearly all probability mass lies in thin strips that constrain only a few orthogonal directions. The authors use this to build agnostic learners for several Boolean multi-index model classes, including functions of halfspaces, and also prove Statistical Query lower bounds. For functions of k halfspaces, the dimension dependence is improved over previous results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Gaussian partitioning and improve dimension dependence for learning multi-index models, with matching SQ lower bounds reported.

entry.title: Logarithmic regret bound for alternating mirror descent in zero-sum games
entry.summary: Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD), a learning rule for zero-sum games. The authors prove that, for two-player zero-sum bilinear games with compact convex strategy sets and mild regularity assumptions on the regularizers, the sum of both players' external regrets is O(log T), which is nearly constant. These assumptions hold for the negative entropy regularizer, so the alternating multiplicative weights update algorithm also attains logarithmic regret. The bound further implies an O(log T / T) duality gap for the averaged strategies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question, proving an O(log T) regret bound for alternating OMD in bilinear zero-sum games and verifying it for the negative entropy regularizer.

entry.title: Differentially private agnostic learning of halfspaces with no extra sample cost
entry.summary: Privacy for Free in Efficient Agnostic Halfspace Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents the first computationally efficient differentially private algorithms for agnostically learning halfspaces. It covers three settings: improper learning under Gaussian and log-concave marginals, proper learning under Gaussian marginals, and semi-agnostic learning under Gaussian marginals. In all three, the extra sample complexity caused by privacy matches the corresponding non-private sample complexity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first efficient differentially private agnostic halfspace learners, with privacy adding no sample complexity beyond non-private bounds.

entry.title: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data
entry.summary: Robust Reconstruction of Power Lines from Incomplete Mobile and Aerial LiDAR Data arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents an automated method for reconstructing individual power conductors from mobile and aerial LiDAR point clouds, even when returns are sparse, incomplete, or occluded by vegetation. It combines scaled density-based clustering, robust polynomial fitting, and iterative fragment merging, applying the same pipeline to both data types without modality-specific tuning. On the aerial dataset it reports 96.87% precision, 96.66% recall, and a 0.127 m geometric RMSE; on the mobile dataset, a 0.045 m point-to-model RMSE and 95.27% coverage. Source code and data are publicly available. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply one modality-agnostic pipeline to mobile and aerial LiDAR power-line reconstruction, reporting 96.87% precision and 96.66% recall on aerial data with degradation and sensitivity expe

entry.title: From Natural to Medical Images: Whether Diffusion Models Transfer to Medical Image Generation
entry.summary: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether diffusion denoisers pretrained on natural images transfer to medical image generation. Experiments span latent and pixel-space paradigms, model sizes from 131M to 952M parameters, and two radiology datasets, RadImageNet and BraTS. Natural-image initialisation consistently improves generation quality, and the benefit tracks spatial structure rather than semantics. The authors conclude that natural-image denoisers transfer positively to medical ones in their setup. ★★★★ Notable: The authors systematically study natural-image transfer to medical diffusion denoisers, identify spatial structure as the key channel, and report 21-34% gFID gains on RadImageNet and BraTS.

entry.title: Provably Learning Mixtures of Linear Experts
entry.summary: Provably Learning Mixtures of Linear Experts arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies whether gradient-based training of Mixture-of-Experts models converges to good solutions. It analyzes a gated mixture with linear experts and a gate defined by Gaussian clusters in the input space, and proves that gradient EM on the likelihood jointly trains the gate and experts to any prescribed accuracy. Under logarithmic overparameterization and a separation condition on gate centers, convergence occurs in polynomially many iterations from random gate initialization and least-squares-initialized experts. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a global convergence guarantee for joint gradient EM training of gated linear-expert mixtures, with experiments on the predicted phase transition.

entry.title: RoboTryOn: Creating Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
entry.summary: RoboTryOn: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On arXiv · Nov 4, 2026RoboTryOn converts human videos into videos of a target robot specified by a reference image, keeping the original task, objects, and background. It translates keyframes autoregressively for visual consistency, then synthesizes video conditioned on the human hand skeleton. An inverse dynamics model using depth features infers action labels from the synthesized videos for policy learning. Policies trained on this synthetic data raised average success on novel tasks from 2% to 60%, at about a third of teleoperation collection cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors treat human-to-robot translation as virtual try-on, synthesizing robot videos for policy learning; the abstract reports bimanual success rising from 2% to 60%.

entry.title: Random matrix analysis of symmetric tensor unfolding, a method for recovering hidden signals from noisy high-order data
entry.summary: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies recovering a hidden unit vector from a spiked tensor corrupted by symmetric Gaussian noise. Instead of replacing the noise with an i.i.d. tensor as earlier work did, the authors analyze the symmetric model directly using random matrix theory. They show that square unfolding undergoes a sharp phase transition at signal strength around n^((p-2)/4), and derive precise expressions for the spectral distribution, threshold, and overlap. ★★★★ Notable: The authors analyze symmetric tensor unfolding directly via random matrix theory, showing a sharp phase transition at λ≍n^{(p-2)/4} and validating an open conjecture.

entry.title: PAC learning where each example has several correct answers
entry.summary: PAC Learning with Multiple Correct Answers arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies PAC learning when each example has at most ℓ correct labels, and a prediction counts as correct if it lies in that set. Training may reveal the full set, only whether a proposed label is correct, or a single correct label chosen by a demonstrator. The authors show that learning from demonstrations can be much harder than learning from full sets or bandit feedback, and they give dimension-based characterizations of learnability for finite and countable label spaces. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize learnability from full sets, bandit feedback and demonstrations, and report a tight ε^{-ℓ} sample bound with proofs for finite and countable label spaces.

entry.title: Learning intersections of degree-2 polynomial threshold functions beyond multi-index models
entry.summary: Beyond Multi-Index Models: Learning Intersections of Degree-2 PTFs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents a PAC learning algorithm for intersections of k degree-2 polynomial threshold functions over R^d under a Gaussian distribution. It achieves error ε in time and samples d^{O(k)}·2^{O_k(log^3(1/ε))}, improving on the d^{O(k^2/ε^2)} running time of polynomial regression. An SQ lower bound shows the d^{Ω(k)} dimension dependence is unavoidable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a learner whose dimension exponent is independent of accuracy, with a matching SQ lower bound for degree-2 PTF intersections.

entry.title: ToolSpace: Tool-centric environment synthesis for training long-horizon AI agents
entry.summary: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026ToolSpace proposes a framework that builds training environments around tools rather than data, mining dependencies between adjacent tool calls from real MCP service execution traces using deterministic rules. It clusters the resulting tool-composition graph into environments and generates tasks via state-aware random walks, keeping only those that replay successfully. On seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks, the method substantially raises the average scores of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and GLM-5.2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose tool-centric environment synthesis mined from execution traces, reporting gains across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks.

entry.title: Unified Theory of Capability Degradation in LLM Fine-Tuning via Feature Interference
entry.summary: Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies Pervasive Capability Degradation (PCD), where supervised fine-tuning of a large language model on a target task erodes general capabilities learned during pre-training. The authors propose a geometric theory attributing PCD to feature interference under superposition, which unifies existing mitigation methods into six paradigms. They also show that cross-entropy with one-hot supervision cannot resolve PCD alone and introduce the AEGIS loss, which constrains activation margin drift across competing tokens. Tested on 14 SFT tasks across 3 model families, AEGIS reportedly performs well on both target and general capabilities at about 1.3 times the cost of standard SFT. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a feature-interference geometric theory unifying six paradigms and a new AEGIS loss, reporting gains over representative methods across 3 model families and 14 tasks.

entry.title: Complexity bounds for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization with exact proximal access
entry.summary: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization with Exact Proximal Oracles arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems, which arise in adversarial training and distributionally robust learning. It shows that neither unrestricted adaptive algorithms nor exact component proximal steps improve the polynomial complexity. The authors give a lower bound on the number of component queries needed to find an epsilon-stationary point, and note that a gradient-only method matches this rate up to a logarithmic factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show exact proximal oracles and unrestricted adaptivity fail to improve polynomial complexity, giving a lower bound matched by a gradient method up to a log factor.

entry.title: Reducing Logprob Without Causal Verification: Checking Whether SAE-Based Methods Really Suppress Personal Data in LLMs
entry.summary: Reducing Logprob Without Causal Verification: Diagnosing SAE-Based PII Suppression in LLMs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines methods that use sparse autoencoder (SAE) feature interventions to stop large language models from leaking personally identifiable information, which are usually judged by how much they lower log-probability. The authors show this measure cannot tell targeted suppression apart from side effects of large activation changes. Across 36 model, layer, and PII-type cases, 17 looked successful on log-probability alone, but only 1 passed their multi-metric framework. The authors propose causally grounded suppression based on circuit-level localization and causal mediation analysis as a new research direction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show logprob reduction cannot separate feature-specific suppression from magnitude artifacts, testing 36 cases against random-direction controls with multiple metrics.

entry.title: What removing a graph edge means: intervention-aware fidelity for GNN explanations
entry.summary: What Does It Mean to Remove an Edge? Intervention-Aware Fidelity for Graph Neural Network Explanations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Graph neural network explanations are often judged by deleting their top-ranked edges and measuring how the model output changes. The paper argues that deleting an edge in message passing can mean two different interventions: structural deletion, which recomputes graph-dependent quantities, and message suppression, which keeps the structure but blocks the edge's message. The authors give conditions under which the two are equivalent and test them on nine datasets with GIN, GCN, and GATv2 models. They find that the relative fidelity of edge rankings often depends on which intervention is used for evaluation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate structural deletion from message suppression, derive exact equivalence conditions, and report that relative fidelity of edge rankings shifts with the evaluation intervention acros

entry.title: Does LinUCB Need Valid Confidence Sets?
entry.summary: Does LinUCB Need Valid Confidence Sets? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper shows that replacing LinUCB's usual confidence width with any fixed positive constant still yields sublinear regret when the action set is M-smooth and m-strongly convex. It gives a high-probability regret bound for this generalised method, α-LinUCB, indicating that valid confidence sets are not required for LinUCB to succeed. The analysis uses a logarithmically capped spectral potential, and at the standard width it gives an O((M/m)d√(T log T)) regret bound, improving the horizon dependence of classical LinUCB by a factor of √log T. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show fixed-width α-LinUCB keeps sublinear regret on smooth strongly convex action sets, introducing a log-capped spectral potential improving the classical bound by √log T.

entry.title: A Benchmark and Model for Judging 3D Gaussian Splatting Video Quality Across Geometry and Color
entry.summary: 3DGS-VBench+ and 3DGSV-Assessor: A Multi-Dimensional Subjective Benchmark and a Reference-Flexible Objective Model for 3D Gaussian Splatting Video Quality Assessment arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses how to assess the quality of videos rendered from 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) models, which are compressed and can suffer distortions in geometry and color. The authors introduce 3DGS-VBench+, a subjective benchmark of 3,036 reconstructions with 9,108 human quality scores covering overall, geometry, and color quality. They also propose 3DGSV-Assessor, a multimodal model that scores all three dimensions in one pass and supports both reduced-reference and no-reference assessment. entry.title: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness
entry.summary: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a method for mathematically formalizing PTX, NVIDIA's GPU intermediate assembly language, to model and reason about common deep learning GPU kernel patterns. These include acquire-release, tensor cores, proxies, async operations, multi-kernel pipelines, and data-dependent control flow. The authors implement the approach in Lean and use it to prove the correctness of simple implementations of a WGMMA GEMM kernel, FlashAttention, and a 3-kernel MoE pipeline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize PTX in Lean, covering tensor cores and async operations, and prove correctness of WGMMA GEMM, FlashAttention, and a MoE pipeline.

entry.title: Entropy-gated adaptive correction for object hallucination in vision-language models
entry.summary: Entropy-Gated Dynamic Rectification for Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large vision-language models sometimes name objects that are not in the image. The paper proposes EGDR, which adjusts an existing latent steering gate's threshold using the entropy of the previous step's logits: high entropy lowers the threshold, while low entropy keeps the calibrated setting. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, it further reduces CHAIR hallucination scores compared with the static gate. It needs no extra forward pass and adds roughly 2% latency. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use predictive entropy as a causally available signal to dynamically set the steering threshold, reporting CHAIR gains on LLaVA-1.5-7B and LLaVA-NeXT-7B with public code.

entry.title: Sketchpad: a small vision-language model with certified exact arithmetic
entry.summary: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents Sketchpad, in which a small vision-language model (Qwen3.5-0.8B with a low-rank adapter) performs arithmetic step by step on a rendered sheet, reading only a three-cell view per step. The authors prove in Lean that exactness on all input lengths reduces to checking a finite set of views. They report that the model solved all 200 pre-registered problems in a web browser and all 220 sums and products tested, outperforming a comparison model on that set. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce exact arithmetic to a finite checkable property, prove it in Lean, and report verification on 2,446 views and several problem sets.

entry.title: Hidden evaluation-tool errors can reorder AI agent leaderboard rankings
entry.summary: Silent Instrument Errors Reorder Agent Leaderboards arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper argues that scores on public agent leaderboards can be distorted by flaws in the evaluation infrastructure, such as grading, cost logging, action recording, and evaluator versioning, without any visible sign. Using two public leaderboards, the authors show cases where re-grading saved results without rerunning agents changes the ordering. They propose checks including reporting the graded fraction, aggregating cost from root spans, tagging the provenance of recorded actions, and pinning evaluator versions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors audit two public agent leaderboards and report three instrument errors that silently reorder rankings, arguing evaluation infrastructure is part of the measurement.

entry.title: Do Conversation Skills Carry From Text to Speech? A Multilingual Benchmark
entry.summary: Do Multi-Turn Conversational Capabilities Carry Over from Text to Speech? A Parallel Multilingual Benchmark arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces Omnilingua-AudioMC, a strictly parallel multilingual extension of Audio MultiChallenge with 354 conversations and 1,404 rubric items across ten languages. It compares six speech-language models on the same conversations given as reference transcripts versus direct speech input. Results show transcript performance is an unreliable proxy for multilingual spoken conversational ability, and that the representation of preceding spoken context is a key source of recoverable degradation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a strictly parallel ten-language benchmark comparing transcript and speech conditions, reporting experiments on six speech-language models and paired rubric analysis.

entry.title: Proper agnostic learning of affine halfspaces under log-concave distributions
entry.summary: Proper Agnostic Learning of Affine Halfspaces under Log-Concave Marginals arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents a proper constant-factor agnostic learner for affine halfspaces under full-dimensional log-concave marginals. It uses independent labeled samples for arbitrary binary labels and returns one affine halfspace with error at most C·OPT+ε. Sample and arithmetic complexity are polynomial in dimension, inverse accuracy, and the log of the inverse failure probability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a proper constant-factor agnostic learner for affine halfspaces under log-concave marginals, with a global-versus-balanced disagreement comparison as the core geometric result and pol

entry.title: How task order affects continual learning: an empirical study and order-aware evaluation for motion forecasting
entry.summary: What Is the Influence of Task Order in Continual Learning? An Empirical Study and Order-Aware Evaluation for Motion Forecasting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how the order of tasks affects continual learning, using four road-layout tasks from the INTERACTION dataset for motion forecasting. It covers all 24 task orders, four algorithms, and three training replicates. Task order accounts for 65% to 91% of the variation in current-task error and backward transfer, and most of this effect comes from which task is learned first. The authors recommend that benchmarks declare their order distribution and report order-resolved and starting-task-resolved results alongside aggregate scores. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose order-aware evaluation of continual learning, reporting 288 runs showing starting task identity dominates order effects in motion forecasting.

entry.title: How Much Risk Does a Data-Driven Policy Carry?
entry.summary: How Risky Is Your Data-Driven Policy? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper measures the risk of data-driven policies using the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of losses over the training sample, policy randomization, and future outcomes. Regret relative to an oracle that knows the distribution splits into post-sample regret and a sample-risk premium. It gives conditions under which the premium vanishes and how large it is relative to post-sample regret, along with convergence rates for sample average approximation in two settings. In finite-sample numerical examples, the premium accounts for roughly 74% to 97% of regret. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decompose data-driven policy regret into post-sample regret and a sample-risk premium, characterize its vanishing conditions, and report numerical SAA examples.

entry.title: Sketch-Omni: A Model That Locates Objects Using Sketches
entry.summary: Sketch-Omni: Instance-Level Sketch-Based Visual Prompting for Perception MLLMs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces Sketch-Omni, described as the first perception multimodal large language model built to work on sketches and from them. It can detect and locate objects within a sketch using text prompts, and can use a drawing of one object to find that specific instance in a photograph, even among similar objects. Training data is generated automatically through edge detection and sketch-to-photo instance pairing rather than hand labeling. The model reports 91.4 F1 on sketch-prompted localisation, compared with 81.8 for the strongest general-purpose multimodal model.</summary> ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a sketch-focused perception MLLM that builds training data automatically via edge detection, reporting gains over general MLLMs on six tasks.

entry.title: Paper on whether two-layer random ReLU networks can separate two disjoint data classes
entry.summary: Two-Layer Random ReLU Networks Can Separate Disjoint Classes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies when two classes of data, not necessarily convex or linearly separable, can be separated with positive margin by finite ReLU networks and by random ReLU features. For deterministic networks, it proves that positive-margin separation is equivalent to the existence of finite closed convex covers, and that exactly two hidden layers suffice. For random features, it gives conditions under which two independent random ReLU layers yield a positive-margin affine separator with high probability. The required width scales quadratically with the largest Gaussian width of a spherical difference-cone section, and an example shows this dependence is sharp. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove exactly two hidden ReLU layers suffice for positive-margin separation and give random-feature width bounds with a tight quadratic Gaussian-width dependence.

entry.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models
entry.summary: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how pushforward measures generated by parameterized families of Lipschitz vector fields can approximate probability measures, motivated by the expressive power of neural ODEs in flow-based generative modeling. For Wasserstein distances, it establishes a quantitative link between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation, with universality criteria based on L^p approximation of transport maps. For total variation, it shows that coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient when d≥2 and gives sufficient conditions based on one-dimensional Sobolev approximation and shear-type mixing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish a quantitative link between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation, with universality criteria for Wasserstein and total variation distances.

entry.title: DreamX: A Video Diffusion Model Used as a Universal Latent Action Learner
entry.summary: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner arXiv · Nov 4, 2026DreamX repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model to learn compact latent actions from video, compressing each latent frame by 300 times (1,200 to 4 tokens). The latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics separated from visual appearance, so they can serve as a shared interface across humans, robots, environments, and action parameterizations. The paper reports state-of-the-art results among latent action models on LARY-Bench, along with any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer.

entry.title: From self-operating AI agents to AI systems that augment human thinking
entry.summary: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper argues that AI should be judged not only by what machines can do alone, but also by how much they can enhance a person's own intelligence, a concept it calls AI-augmented human intelligence. It proposes a "cognitive symbiont," a lifelong companion that senses what its user senses, keeps their context over time, and joins their thinking and everyday tasks at the right moments. The authors also note new risks such systems raise, and treat their governance as part of the paradigm.

entry.title: Aligning language models to general preferences via direct Nash optimization: an empirical study
entry.summary: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) and its practical variant DNO-Prct, which align a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. The authors re-implement the method on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, reporting higher length-controlled win rates on AlpacaEval 2.0 after three iterations. The paper also includes ablations, pipeline cost, and a discussion of single-run results and GPT-4o serving as both teacher and judge.

entry.title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Robot Imitation Learning
entry.summary: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Robot imitation learning usually depends on costly real-world teleoperation data, and unguided collection often yields data that adds little to policy performance. The paper proposes GUILD, which alternates between proposing tasks with vision-language model priors and collecting data, and evaluating the collected trajectories via predictive data attribution to see how they affect performance on a target deployment setting. This feedback guides subsequent collection. Experiments in simulation and on real robots report improved sample efficiency and deployment performance over passive collection and several baselines.

entry.title: Visibility-aware reference generation for benchmarking 3D reconstruction in vegetated scenes
entry.summary: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a LiDAR-based pipeline that generates reference depth maps and visible point clouds from existing multi-sensor localization datasets. It introduces the LDGVS visibility score for point-wise filtering and automatic scale selection in Hidden Point Removal. On TartanAirV2 and TartanGround, the method retains about three times the point density of Poisson surface reconstruction at comparable absolute relative error. Applied to BotanicGarden, it compares feed-forward and conventional SfM methods, finding that feed-forward methods are efficient but can duplicate structures, while SfM yields coherent but sparse geometry that is more prone to failure in vegetated scenes.

entry.title: GSCV++: A lightweight method for compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting sequences with standard video codecs
entry.summary: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline that compresses 3D Gaussian Splatting sequences using standard video codecs. It improves three stages: preprocessing through energy-adaptive reduction of spherical harmonic coefficients, 3D-to-2D mapping via prior-based P-MiniPLAS, and content-aware compression settings. Experiments report over 20% intra- and 60% inter-prediction rate-distortion gains over state-of-the-art methods, along with faster 2D map generation, encoding, and decoding.

entry.title: Durably Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models
entry.summary: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how to suppress undesired behaviors that appear in language models after training, comparing SFT, GRPO, and gradient-ascent unlearning on immediate suppression, durability under further training, and retained capability. It introduces PEARL, a GRPO variant that augments rollouts with continuations from intermediate states along cached trajectories. Across two model families and two misbehaving model organisms, PEARL achieves strong immediate suppression while preserving task accuracy and staying durable under further fine-tuning.

entry.title: Adversarial speculative decoding to improve long-horizon AI agents
entry.summary: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper argues that speculative decoding affects more than speed, since it can shift the output distribution and reasoning accuracy of long-horizon agents. The authors train a draft model to be rejected at critical reasoning points, so that those tokens are sampled from the target model under less noisy conditions. On complex agentic coding benchmarks, the method raises end-to-end success rate without changing the target model or its output distribution.

entry.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
entry.summary: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study tests whether a language model, given only a clinical protocol and a small network's raw weights, can audit and repair that network. Planted flaws included confounds, a 3 Gy cord threshold shift, and a hidden trigger in networks screening head-and-neck radiotherapy planning requests. The model named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks and repaired them, but found only 1 of 3 triggers and cleared 2 of 5 healthy networks. The authors conclude it can locate some flaws but cannot yet certify a network as correct.

entry.title: A parameter-free accelerated optimization method for convex problems using p-norm preconditioning
entry.summary: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in p-norm geometry arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method (A²ODA) for unconstrained convex optimization, using low-cost preconditioning based on p-norm geometry for p in [2, ∞]. The method requires no line search and selects stepsizes with a new technique based on an aggregated affine lower model. Its update structure is unified across p and is no more complicated for p > 2 than for the Euclidean case p = 2. Under a generalized local smoothness condition, the authors derive a convergence bound, and in the special case of local smoothness it recovers a nearly optimal rate.

entry.title: CATF: A manager-worker framework for forecasting time series using context
entry.summary: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies forecasting a time series from its own history plus contextual variables such as weather and calendar data. The authors propose CATF, in which a Transformer-based manager sends each input to a single worker model based on its context, using hard routing in training and inference so workers specialize without manual data splitting. On five context-rich datasets, CATF beats its standalone versions in 162 of 200 comparisons and outperforms the zero-shot Time-MoE model in 15 of 20 settings.

entry.title: HARP: A training-free dual-profile agent communication method for LLM-based recommendation
entry.summary: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper frames LLM-based recommendation as an agentic communication process with four stages: building a self-description, transmitting it along the collaborative graph, understanding the other side, and synchronizing from the next interaction. It proposes HARP, a training-free method that adds three operators to a frozen LLM backbone: a symmetric item profile, a profile-level homophily measure used at retrieval, and a single-pass reflective update. On four public benchmarks (Yelp, Books, MovieTV, Goodreads), HARP raises Hit@1 by 6.9% to 24.0% over the strongest published baseline.

entry.title: MDSKILL: A method that helps AI agents absorb stored skills more efficiently by training on three types of skill views.
entry.summary: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026MDSKILL organizes an agent's skill memories into three functional views: state grounding, action planning, and execution control. It selects high-quality skills using dynamic metrics and builds reasoning branches for each view and for their integration. On-Policy Self-Distillation then transfers these branches' knowledge into a shared policy, and the paper reports gains of up to 7.1% on ALFWorld and 8.1% on WebShop over prior state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: ΦasmaNet: a fast neural network that predicts gravitational-wave signal strength
entry.summary: ΦasmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces ΦasmaNet, a compact neural network that predicts the signal-to-noise ratio of gravitational waves from binary black holes without computing full waveforms. It is evaluated for a single detector at Advanced LIGO design sensitivity, using about 732k parameters. The authors report it processes a million-signal catalogue in about 8.3 seconds on one GPU, roughly two orders of magnitude faster than conventional methods on a 16-core CPU.

entry.title: A study on whether language models need long context, using frequent compaction to keep contexts short
entry.summary: You don't need long context arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper notes that later tokens cost more to generate than earlier ones, with the cost gap on frontier open-weight models reaching up to 7x. Through frequent compaction, the authors show that across many long-horizon and long-input tasks, models keep little to no accuracy when contexts stay short. They also report that performance on long-horizon software engineering tasks does not collapse even with at most one action per context, and outline semantic state space models (SSSMs) as a concept, questioning the need for long-context models.

entry.title: LoopVQ: Sub-1-Bit KV Cache Compression for Looped Transformers
entry.summary: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Looped transformers reuse the same layers across several loop steps to save parameters, but each step still stores its own key-value (KV) cache, which becomes the main memory bottleneck. This paper proposes LoopVQ, which jointly codes channels across loop steps and fine-tunes codebooks to match full-precision outputs. At 0.5 bits per element, it outperforms existing KV cache vector quantization methods on Ouro and Huginn models across several task types. Its SGLang implementation nearly halves decode latency at 32K context and improves peak serving throughput.

entry.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
entry.summary: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes GSBR, a regularization method for online reinforcement learning that penalizes actions by their distance from the support of a pretrained base policy. Actions inside the support are not penalized, while outside the support the penalty grows smoothly with distance, allowing improvement when the gained value outweighs it. Across 19 tasks on four robotic benchmarks, GSBR raises the average success rate from 33% for the base policy to 95%, with the highest average success rate and throughput among compared methods.

entry.title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Method for Image Quality Enhancement
entry.summary: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Real photos often suffer from several defects at once, such as blur, grain, compression, scratches, and low resolution, each with different severity and location. Wonder 4 is a mixture-of-experts model that corrects these defects simultaneously in the regions where they occur, without using a degradation classifier, mask, prompt, or task label. Each block holds 13 experts, and a router sends every image patch to 5 of them, trained with a bias that only sets a minimum usage share rather than forcing equal use. On DIV2K and Flickr2K, it achieves the best LPIPS, DISTS, and NIQE scores across all three test settings.

entry.title: "Personas Are Not People": Limits of Fixed Synthetic Personas for Simulating Populations
entry.summary: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines the use of synthetic populations, simulated people defined by fixed persona profiles, in place of real people for survey pretesting and AI evaluation. The authors argue that behavior varies more across contexts than between people, so fixed personas cannot reproduce the context-specific part of a population's behavior, however detailed or large the model. They propose a new evaluation criterion and a person-in-context design, tested on a Reddit personality corpus and a clinical-trial recruitment survey. The design produces context-dependent behavior but does not fully match the real populations.

entry.title: Classifying sparse 3D point clouds with a new network that stays accurate at low density
entry.summary: Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the problem of classifying 3D point clouds when their density is low, a condition that can degrade existing methods. It introduces LD-PointNet++, an architecture optimized for low-density point cloud classification. The authors also present the first benchmark that systematically compares state-of-the-art methods across varying densities, showing significant performance declines at low density. Experiments on the ModelNet dataset show LD-PointNet++ outperforms these methods in low-density scenarios and keeps accuracy above 90% across density levels.

entry.title: Anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning to make pretrained place recognition models robust to attacks
entry.summary: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Visual place recognition locates a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images. The paper shows that current foundation-model methods such as SuperVLAD and BoQ are highly vulnerable to tiny adversarial perturbations. The authors propose ARAFT, which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss and an anchor to the frozen model's clean descriptors, and report improved robust recall under a fixed clean-accuracy budget.

entry.title: YANAMI: A large-scale multimodal dataset and benchmark for multi-turn stateful dialogue.
entry.summary: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces YANAMI, comprising YANAMI-400K, a dataset of 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogues, and YANAMI-Bench, a benchmark of 400 dialogues. The dialogues cover four scenarios (multi-image fusion, image editing, world modeling, and visual reasoning) and require models to track and revise evolving dialogue states across turns. Fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improved image editing by 10.3%, generation by 2.0%, and stateful interaction by 13.23%, while evaluations show existing models still struggle with this task.

entry.title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model for Understanding and Generation
entry.summary: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents Möbius, a single model that understands, generates, and edits human motion within one framework. It brings the diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for understanding and operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, without discrete tokenization or a pretrained motion VAE. According to the paper, it achieves state-of-the-art results among unified motion models on HumanML3D and scales to 1.7B parameters with 1,700 hours of motion data.

entry.title: Neural network method for physics problems with holes, using de Rham cohomology
entry.summary: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes Hodge-de Rham PINNs, a variant of physics-informed neural networks augmented with de Rham cohomology, to handle problems with topological features such as holes and punctures. The method parameterizes a 1-form using the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs decomposition and links it to scalar PDE solutions through integral operators. The authors test the approach on problems including the Aharonov-Bohm effect and provide theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: iGC: Reinforcement learning for antibody optimization using a learned mutation prior
entry.summary: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning framework for optimizing antibodies against specific antigens. The first stage learns a somatic hypermutation (SHM) prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. The second stage initializes a policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with KL regularization, using a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective to prevent reward exploitation.

entry.title: Stabilizing targeted guidance in agentic reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies targeted guidance, a method that learns from per-turn textual feedback through an on-policy self-distillation objective, to improve behaviors that are hard to optimize with reinforcement learning. The authors test the approach in an agentic multi-turn software engineering environment. They report that combining targeted self-distillation with a per-criteria RL reward, and giving feedback only on turns where the policy fails, works well. The paper also examines design choices that keep entropy stable and reduce oscillation during training.

entry.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A joint hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for multi-step web tasks
entry.summary: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces JHiMA-WebRL, which trains a task decomposer and an action-executing actor jointly so web agents can handle long, multi-step tasks on websites. The decomposer is initially fine-tuned on structured subtask annotations produced by a strong teacher model from multimodal GUI trajectories, and both components are then optimized together with an extended GRPO method in the WebArena environment. On WebArena-Lite-v2, the 14B model (a 7B actor with a 7B decomposer) reaches a 37.2% average success rate, compared with 24% for a ScaleCUA-32B agent trained with RL on the same tasks. Ablations indicate that updating the decomposer during RL performs better than updating the actor alone.

entry.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice
entry.summary: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents NovoCRF, a conditional random field whose states are prefix masses, for de novo peptide sequencing from mass spectrometry data. It is trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible peptides and uses exact k-best decoding plus two BiGRU rerankers. On seven held-out 2026 datasets, it reports higher peptide and amino-acid recall than Casanovo v5 and much higher throughput.

entry.title: "Going Deeper With Memories": a multiscale byte-level language model with memory blocks
entry.summary: Going Deeper With Memories arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces DeepMem, a causal multiscale architecture for byte-level language modeling that uses a learned invertible subband transform to compress byte sequences into shorter representations while preserving byte identity through a lossless carrier and detail sidebands. It adds fast weight memory blocks in the encoder, iterative shared state computation at the compressed bottleneck, and an attention-based super-resolution decoder that restores byte-level representations. The authors report stronger language modeling than a matched byte-level Transformer on FineWeb-Edu and PG19, and the best macro average across evaluated FLORES languages.

entry.title: Shrinkage Priors for Implicit Generative Models
entry.summary: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a sample-efficient training method for implicit generative models built on deep neural networks. It combines regularized inference with shrinkage priors and the generalized Bayes framework, using a scoring rule posterior based on a strictly proper scoring rule. The authors introduce a block SGMCMC within Gibbs sampling to explore high-dimensional parameter spaces and identify sparse representations of these models. Performance is demonstrated on linear regression with p ≫ n and on an application to neural generative models.

entry.title: Post-stratified importance sampling: a method that improves importance sampling estimates by reducing them to one-dimensional modeling.
entry.summary: Post-stratified importance sampling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Importance sampling estimates can have very high or infinite variance, and their empirical standard errors are often unreliable. Inspired by multilevel regression and poststratification in survey sampling, the authors propose post-stratified importance sampling (PIS), which turns high-dimensional weighting into two one-dimensional problems: regression for the conditional mean of the importance ratio and density estimation for its marginal law. Ordinary importance sampling is a special case. A model-based implementation uses one-dimensional Gaussian process regression and heavy-tailed density estimation, and simulations and cross-validation applications show gains in estimation accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: ARLoop: Fully Open Pretrained Looped Transformers Using Attention Residuals
entry.summary: ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes ARLoop, a looped transformer that repeatedly applies shared layers and selectively reuses earlier layer outputs through attention over depth. The authors find that sliding-window depth attention matches or beats full-history attention at larger recurrent depths. Scaled to 1.2B parameters and pretrained on 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, the model outperforms Huginn-3.5B on all evaluated tasks, with especially strong gains in math and coding.

entry.title: Diagnosis by Composition: Finding and Locating Unseen Diseases from Combined Radiological Findings
entry.summary: Diagnosis by Composition: Detecting and Localizing Unseen Diseases by Composing Learned Radiological Findings arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces diagnosis by composition (DbC), a learning framework that mirrors how radiologists move from visual findings to disease through guidelines. The model learns a vocabulary of radiological findings, and each disease is defined by its required findings, combined without learned parameters into a diagnosis map. On multi-phase liver CT, DbC detects and localizes unseen diseases, rare diseases from another institution, and external cohorts better than all comparators.

entry.title: Regret-based characterization, information limits, and auditing sample complexity for adaptive policies
entry.summary: Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies whether a policy's performance comes from its average action placement or from reacting to information in a finite-horizon MDP. It shows that the gap between a policy and its open-loop marginal equals a sum of covariance terms, and bounds this gap by the information the policy uses. The authors also give the number of rounds needed to estimate this gap from bandit-feedback logs, and provide an importance-sampling auditor for episodic MDPs.

entry.title: Post-Inference Model Chaining: A Problem Statement and a Model-based Bootstrap for Training End-to-End Digital Twins
entry.summary: Post-Inference Model Chaining: A Problem Statement and a Model-based Bootstrap for Training End-to-End Digital Twins arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines how separately fitted stage models are chained after inference to build end-to-end digital twins, and how a common Monte Carlo simulation approach behaves when predictions are forwarded through such chains. Analytical examples and simulations of multi-stage linear-quadratic chains show interval and coverage inflation, along with input-dependent bias. The authors propose a model-based bootstrap, which in the tested scenarios substantially reduces relative mean bias and brings coverage closer to the nominal 90%.

entry.title: Learning curves in natural and artificial systems: a unified mathematical model
entry.summary: Learning curves in natural and artificial systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a general model of experience formation, defining the learning level as the probability that the next uncertainty value has been mastered and not forgotten. It derives that the learning curve shape is mainly determined by the distribution of situation occurrence, giving exponential curves for uniform distributions and power-law curves for power-law distributions. The authors relate these mechanisms to scaling laws in deep learning and address choosing a training distribution that differs from the deployment distribution.

entry.title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions
entry.summary: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces PLANTEUR, a benchmark for mapping crop types from satellite images in French overseas territories. It provides aligned Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8 image sequences with parcel-based labels covering six tropical regions and eight classes. The authors define a standard test split and a leave-one-island-out protocol to measure generalization across territories, and they evaluate fully supervised models, linear probes, and fine-tuned foundation models. The code and data are open source on GitHub and Hugging Face.

entry.title: AUC-based fairness measures for clinical prediction AI
entry.summary: Fairness Metrics based on the AUC in Clinical Predictive AI arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines eight AUC-based fairness metrics used to compare clinical prediction models for binary outcomes across subgroups. It explains that AUC is non-collapsible, so subgroup and overall AUC values cannot be directly compared, and analyses what each metric estimates. Simulations based on the EuroSCORE II in-hospital mortality model illustrate their behaviour. The authors recommend reporting an AUC matrix and, when needed, within-group AUC parity.

entry.title: Predicting flood peak depth from high-water marks using terrain, satellite embeddings and weather data
entry.summary: Fusing Earth observation embeddings and spaceborne terrain with meteorological forcing for flood peak depth prediction from high-water marks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper trains a fusion network on 5,689 USGS high-water mark surveys from 39 flood events to predict flood depth at surveyed sites six hours before the peak. It reports a mean absolute error of 0.39 m, compared with 0.93 m from differencing measured water levels against the same elevation model. On eleven held-out events, however, the model does not resolve depth at the marks (R2 = 0.03).

entry.title: Physics-informed reduced models for multiscale systems using Mori-Zwanzig methods
entry.summary: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper applies the Mori-Zwanzig formalism, a model reduction approach, to bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning rather than standard functions like Fourier modes. The fluctuation-dissipation theorem is used to close the resulting non-Markovian equations for the learned basis coefficients. The authors also introduce a complementary generative closure model. Both closures substantially improve predictions of filtered states compared with Markovian dynamics alone.

entry.title: Multi-objective generative design via expected hypervolume fine-tuning
entry.summary: Multi-Objective Generative Optimization via Expected Hypervolume Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces Hypervolume Fine-Tuning (HVFT), a method that adapts a pretrained generative model so its samples better balance several competing properties. It optimizes the expected hypervolume of generated samples, rewarding both candidate quality and collective trade-off coverage, while keeping the model close to its pretrained distribution via a KL constraint. The authors report state-of-the-art expected hypervolume and trade-off coverage on therapeutic-peptide and molecular design tasks using discrete diffusion and flow-matching models.

entry.title: UltraDiff: Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration Using Diffusion Priors
entry.summary: Diffusion Plug-in Priors for Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents UltraDiff, a method that jointly increases the resolution and removes speckle noise from ultrasound videos without paired training data or network retraining. It uses a frozen pre-trained diffusion model as a plug-in prior and optimizes each frame's sampler seed under a range-constrained maximum a posteriori formulation, with a speckle-aware fidelity term and a total-variation regularizer. On EchoNet-LVH videos, it improves PSNR by 1.24 dB over the strongest baseline, and on real echocardiography videos it reduces the mean absolute error of zero-shot ejection fraction prediction from 7.31 to 6.37 points.

entry.title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Queries for End-to-End Multi-Object Tracking
entry.summary: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes TAQ-MOTR, a framework that forms detection queries in end-to-end multi-object tracking with awareness of trajectory states. A pre-decoder Hybrid Query Generator fuses current-frame image features, track memory, and learnable memory to help discover untracked objects and complement tracked ones. A training-only auxiliary detection branch adds extra detection supervision. The method reports improvements on DanceTrack, SportsMOT, and BFT, reaching 72.0 HOTA, 63.1 AssA, and 76.6 IDF1 on the DanceTrack test set.

entry.title: Empirical Bayes flow matching for continuous cryo-EM structural heterogeneity
entry.summary: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to learn generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, focusing on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy. It proposes Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), which learns a flow matching prior directly from observations by alternating guided flow-based posterior sampling with model updates. The method is validated on two-moons and MNIST inverse problems and on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, where it recovers continuous distributions of protein conformations in atomic-coordinate space.

entry.title: Ensembles of random partition models under covariate shift
entry.summary: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies covariate shift, where the input distribution changes between training and deployment, and why ensembles tend to be more robust than single models. The authors extend covariate shift severity theory from single models to ensembles and introduce new discrepancy measures to control the risk of partition-based kernel estimators. They show that with sufficiently large ensemble size, these models can reach minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. The results suggest that larger ensembles are needed as covariate shift becomes more severe.

entry.title: Factorized MLLM embeddings that model intended edits for composed image retrieval (FactEmbed)
entry.summary: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses composed image retrieval, which finds a target image from a reference image plus a modification text. It proposes FactEmbed, which separates understanding the composed query from building discriminative embeddings, using factorized latents that imagine the intended visual changes. These latents are trained with a factor-level contrastive loss and distilled into a deeper attention layer of the MLLM. The authors report that FactEmbed outperforms prior methods across CIR benchmarks.

entry.title: Adjusting learning rates for cross-entropy training using local quadratic estimates
entry.summary: Stepsize modulation for cross entropy from local quadratic optimization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents two methods that adjust an existing learning rate schedule for stochastic gradient descent with cross-entropy loss, each using one extra forward pass to estimate loss derivatives. Both methods yield very similar step sizes, which are used to slightly raise or lower the scheduled learning rate. Experiments training ResNets on Cifar10 and Cifar100 show faster loss decrease and greater monotonicity than the perturbed schedule. Test accuracy improves slightly on Cifar10 and stays the same on Cifar100.

entry.title: What the Model Sees: Input Choice Validity in AI Video Analysis
entry.summary: What Does the Model See? Representation Validity in Multimodal LLM-Based Video Analysis arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines how social scientists using multimodal large language models to analyze video should choose among text, audio, video, and combined inputs. The authors compare these input representations across six open-weight models and three human-annotated video datasets. They find that no single representation performs best consistently, combining inputs rarely helps, and higher classification accuracy does not reliably yield estimates closer to human codes. The authors conclude that input representations must be validated both for the construct measured and for the estimated quantities derived from the labels.

entry.title: PadLoc: Training-free sensor localization on floor plans using sparse geometric matching
entry.summary: PadLoc: Training-Free Floor-Plan Localization by Sparse Geometric Matching arXiv · Nov 4, 2026PadLoc is a training-free localization back-end that places a moving sensor within a known floor plan. It keeps a swappable depth front-end but replaces the dense pose grid with sparse matching: dominant wall orientations generate a small set of pose candidates, which are scored against free space in the plan and filtered with a Gaussian-mixture Bayes filter. The authors report that it matches or beats competing methods on Gibson trajectories and on Bonn LiLocBench and Hilti-Trimble datasets.

entry.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Optimizing Laser Powder Bed Fusion Processes with Spatter and Defect Awareness
entry.summary: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents AgentAM, a large language model agent that lets process engineers query CFD-trained surrogate models of spatter and melt pool geometry for SS316L via natural language. The polynomial surrogates, trained on 279 single-track simulations, predict melt pool dimensions and spatter volume, and geometric criteria assign defect regimes.
