The agent selects tools for prediction, process-window scans and constrained optimization, and was evaluated on a 145-prompt benchmark.

entry.title: Learning Behavior-Related Brain Dynamics from Multimodal Neural Recordings
entry.summary: Learning Behaviorally Relevant Dynamics in Multimodal Neural Recordings arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents BREM-NET, a nonlinear multimodal dynamical model that fuses spiking activity, local field potentials, and behavior. A structured learning framework separates behaviorally relevant neural dynamics from residual dynamics. On a public non-human primate dataset with simultaneous spiking and LFP recordings during a 2D reaching task, the model shows better behavior decoding, neural prediction, and latent alignment with behavior. It maintains these results when neural modalities are asynchronous or have dropouts.

entry.title: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial QA: When Self-Checking Backfires
entry.summary: When Self-Verification Hurts: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial Question Answering arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies financial question answering, where a model may pull a plausible number from the evidence but attach it to the wrong entity, period, unit, or accounting concept. It proposes Calibrated Answer Repair (CAR), which first estimates whether a draft is likely to benefit from repair, then runs a targeted check, localizes the relevant evidence or draft span, and limits the permitted edit. Across FinRank, Fin-RATE, and FinQA with three open-weight models, CAR outperforms generic verification in all settings, recovering 14.6% of initially missed answer requirements while damaging 2.1% of initially correct ones.

entry.title: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling
entry.summary: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Basin2Vec, a self-supervised framework that learns compact basin representations from hydroclimatic and physiographic data without requiring observed streamflow. Across several forecasting architectures, it outperforms predefined attributes and general-purpose geospatial embeddings in temporal generalization and zero-shot spatial transfer. The authors report average relative gains of up to 8.3% temporally and median predictive performance 3.5 times that of the strongest baselines on unseen basins.

entry.title: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding
entry.summary: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces PROVE, a self-play framework that trains vision-language verifiers to judge whether images match their text descriptions. Starting from a correct image-caption pair, a Mutator perturbs objects, attributes, counts, or relations, the verifier judges the altered caption and gives feedback, and a Repairer restores a faithful caption for re-verification. Experiments report improved fine-grained compositional verification across model scales and families, with limited and benchmark-dependent changes on broader multimodal tasks.

entry.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Fast, data-efficient neural stand-ins for physics simulations
entry.summary: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces macrocanonical generator networks, a method for training fast neural surrogates that reproduce the multiscale statistics of stationary physical processes. The generator is trained to satisfy these statistical constraints in expectation, so realistic sample-to-sample fluctuations are preserved, and each new sample then takes a single forward pass. Experiments on cosmology and fluid simulations show realistic samples can be recovered from very small training sets, with generation far faster than the reference simulator.

entry.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies: Running Reasoning and Action Generation at Separate Rates
entry.summary: Asynchronous Robot Policies arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Large vision-language models improve general robot manipulation, but their computational latency slows real-time physical reactions. The paper proposes Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), which decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation: a high-capacity vision-language model updates a semantic memory at low frequency, while a lightweight vision-action expert generates actions at a much higher control frequency. On Franka manipulation tasks, the authors report higher success rates and shorter execution times than baselines. They also state that the vision-language model can run at about 10 times lower than its nominal frequency with no significant performance loss.

entry.title: Boosting Interactive HTML Generation with High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses generating interactive HTML pages from natural-language specifications, noting that current models often fail to ensure functionality and visual quality during real interaction. Using mini-games as a test setting, the authors propose WebCatalyst, a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework. It combines a game-level GUI assessor, Visual Anchor to mitigate VLM reward hacking, and Action-Trace Credit for runtime-grounded credit assignment.

entry.title: Creating Power Flexibility in Datacenters via Query Routing
entry.summary: Creating Power Flexibility in Datacenters via Query Routing arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Large language model inference is raising datacenter power demand, so facilities need ways to adjust consumption while still serving interactive users. This paper proposes query routing, which spreads queries across model instances without deferring them, and presents an analytical framework linking arrival rates and sequence lengths to power consumption. Validated on four GPU platforms, the framework was tested in a trace-driven simulation of a 10,000 H100 GPU datacenter, showing flexibility up to 16% of total power, with 90% of the desired reduction reached in about 10 seconds.

entry.title: GM League Arena: A Benchmark for Long-Term Sports Team Management by AI Models
entry.summary: GM League Arena: An Interactive Long-Horizon Task Benchmark Based on Professional Sports League Management arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces GM Bench, a benchmark that tests large language models acting as general managers of professional sports teams across multiple seasons under resource limits and competition. It builds simulators for four sports, adding financial constraints, player demands, and market mechanics. Over five NBA seasons, Claude Opus 5.5 ranked first among 29 evaluated LLMs.

entry.title: Beyond Foundation Models: Using PFN Priors to Tune Ordinary Tabular Models
entry.summary: Beyond Foundation Models: PFN Priors Improve Tabular Hyperparameter Optimization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes PriorTune, a method that uses synthetic data priors originally built for pretraining tabular foundation models to select hyperparameter settings for conventional tabular models. Offline, it picks the subset of configurations that wins most often against a random baseline on synthetic datasets, and online it only tries those selected settings on a new dataset. On the BeyondArena benchmark, LightGBM with TabPrep features and these configurations ranks above TabPFN-3 and RealMLP, while being more efficient at inference.

entry.title: Meta²: Precomputed Reusable Knowledge for Adapting Agent Harnesses Online
entry.summary: Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces Meta², a method for improving long-horizon AI agents by optimizing the harness, which consists of prompts, tools, memory, and hooks around a frozen model. Offline, it learns a reusable textual Meta-Skill by contrasting training runs with and without an evolver, guiding when to change the harness and which edits to avoid. Online, an evolver uses this guidance and emerging run evidence to either keep the harness unchanged or make task-local edits. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE 1.1 with GPT-5.6-Terra, Meta² achieves the highest reported performance among evaluated methods, at 81.00% and 44.44%.

entry.title: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments in AI-Drafted Proposals
entry.summary: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments and Silent Choices in AI-Mediated Proposals arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether large language models that turn citizens' opinions into collective proposals produce stable task assignments when the same opinions are processed again. Testing four models on opinions from DeliberationBank and Polis, the authors found that 17% to 20% of five-run sets showed assignments in some runs but not others. Variation persisted under safeguards such as temperature zero, and prompts seeking agreement covered minority positions less than prompts asking to describe differences.

entry.title: Training-free mapping of solar panel modules from multi-view drone images
entry.summary: High-fidelity training-free photovoltaic module mapping from multi-view UAV imagery arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents MV-PVMapper, a training-free framework that maps individual photovoltaic modules by combining vision foundation models with drone photogrammetry. It generates segmentation candidates with SAM 3, projects them into object space with slope correction, and selects instances across views using module-size checks, then feeds accepted results back for iterative refinement. On surveys of three rooftop PV plants, it recovered 7,710 of 7,711 reference modules with no false positives, reaching an aggregated Jaccard index of 97.55%.

entry.title: Solving the nonlinear Westervelt equation for ultrasound using physics-informed neural networks
entry.summary: Solving the Nonlinear Westervelt Equation in Ultrasound Propagation Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper solves the one-dimensional Westervelt equation, which describes finite-amplitude ultrasound propagation in biological tissue, using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). It tests three synthetic cases: linear, shock-dominated, and dissipation-dominated. A sinusoidal activation function is used to capture oscillatory behavior. The results indicate that the attenuation coefficient controls the rate of amplitude decay, while the nonlinearity coefficient governs frequency-dependent phase speeds.

entry.title: Do ray-traced city models beat standard channel priors for unseen base stations? A pre-registered simulation study and a reversed test on measured data
entry.summary: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper asks whether a channel prior pooled from many ray-traced city scenes serves a newly deployed base station better than standard 3GPP CDL models. In simulation, the pooled prior was about 0.6 dB behind a site-trained estimator, roughly matching CDL after 50 measurements, and learned models added little. On measured outdoor channels from the DICHASUS dataset, the result reversed, with the ray-traced prior 3.2 to 4.1 dB worse than CDL.

entry.title: Having the Right Source Is Not Enough: Why Old Audio Distorts Speech AI Answers
entry.summary: The Right Source Is Not Enough: Understanding History Interference in Speech-LLM Memory arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies why irrelevant earlier audio in a multi-turn conversation changes a speech large language model's answers, even when the queried event is still represented. Controlled experiments on MOSS-Audio and MiMo-Audio show that historical values steer errors toward specific competing answers. Causal interventions find that in open-ended question answering most such errors vanish when later computation cannot access the irrelevant source, while many errors persist in multiple-choice answering. The authors conclude that reliable conversational memory requires controlling how retained information enters answer computation, not just retaining and retrieving it.

entry.title: Optimal control theory for early-exit neural networks: turnpikes in ResNets
entry.summary: Towards an Optimal Control Foundation of Early Exits - Turnpikes and ResNets arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper analyzes jointly optimizing losses at the output and intermediate layers of neural networks using optimal control theory. It proves that ResNets trained this way exhibit a turnpike phenomenon, where the layers needed to reach a set loss level are bounded regardless of total depth. The authors connect this to overthinking and explain early-exit criteria based on softmax probabilities, with experiments confirming the effects.

entry.title: Distributed bandit learning for freshness-aware data preprocessing in edge-enabled digital twins
entry.summary: Distributed Linear Bandits for Freshness-Aware Preprocessing in MEC-Enabled Digital Twin Networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies freshness-aware preprocessing of IoT data in digital twin networks supported by multi-access edge computing (MEC) servers, which reduces transmission volume and DT-server load. CPU-allocation selection is formulated as a fixed-confidence distributed best-arm identification problem in linear bandits, solved with the DistLinGapE collaborative learning method. Numerical results indicate the method identifies the optimal feasible strategy and reduces preprocessing delay under stationary task assignments and workloads. In the evaluated settings, collaboration gives an identification speedup nearly proportional to the number of participating MEC servers.

entry.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do AI Agents Learn Across Tasks?
entry.summary: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces CONTINUAL AUTORESEARCH, an environment that compares a persistent AI agent against a reset version of the same agent on matched task streams, data, and time budgets. It covers nine task families, including synthetic tasks, symbolic regression, time-series forecasting, and tabular AutoML, and tests five frontier agents. Persistent state improves research efficiency for all five agents, helping them find stronger solutions sooner, but these gains do not consistently yield better final solutions.

entry.title: Label-preserving Fourier domain adaptation using generative-AI images for 3D mitral valve segmentation
entry.summary: Label-Preserving Fourier Domain Adaptation with Generative-AI and Real Style Donors for 3D Mitral Valve Segmentation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of segmenting the mitral valve in 3D transesophageal echocardiography, where expert-annotated public datasets are scarce. The authors test Fourier Domain Adaptation using images from general generative-AI platforms as annotation-free style sources, comparing them against real-image style donors and other training conditions on the MVSeg2023 dataset. Generative-AI-based adaptation significantly reduced boundary and surface errors, but its effect on Generalized Dice Score depended on the generator, with only MAI showing a significant gain over the baseline. The non-AI control performed comparably to ChatGPT, so the authors do not conclude that the generative approach is superior to using real-image donors.

entry.title: Optical circuit switching set once per deployment to speed up large language model inference decoding
entry.summary: Workload-Static Optical Circuit Switching For Scalable LLM Inference Decode arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses how communication latency during LLM inference decoding limits per-user interactivity in scale-up fabrics built from electronic packet switches. It proposes workload-static optical circuit switching, which configures circuits once per deployment and co-designs them with model parallelism and topology-aware collective schedules. Evaluated with the GXNET emulator on a 576-accelerator domain serving 5T-parameter MoE models, the all-optical fabrics improve interactivity by up to 65% and energy efficiency by up to 119% over 4:1 oversubscribed packet-switched fabrics.

entry.title: Molecular Prior Networks: Predicting Drug-Target Affinity in a Single Forward Pass
entry.summary: Molecular Prior Networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a new approach to modelling drug-target affinity, in which a transformer predicts the labels of query molecules from labelled support molecules in one forward pass. The model is trained on thousands of existing affinity datasets, so it can learn general patterns of molecular activity across targets, chemical series and dataset sizes. For the smallest support sets, it matches the state of the art on the regression variant of the FS-Mol benchmark and runs faster because it requires no task-specific training.

entry.title: Measuring vertical continuity of forest fuel layers using Gaussian decomposition of laser scan point clouds
entry.summary: Characterizing the vertical continuity of fuel strata based on TLS point clouds Gaussian decomposition and overlap metrics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study applies Gaussian decomposition to vertical height profiles from terrestrial laser scanning point clouds across 25 permanent forest plots. It compares geometric, probabilistic, and overlap metrics at multiple spatial scales to characterize vertical fuel continuity. The authors report that 3 to 6 m cells offer a useful compromise, and suggest the approach can improve ladder fuel characterization in wildfire risk assessment.

entry.title: Dual-VaDE: Stable, Robust Medical Image Prototype Learning Using Dual-Domain Priors
entry.summary: Dual-VaDE: Efficient and Robust Prototype Learning via Variational Dual-Domain Mixture Priors arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Dual-VaDE is an unsupervised generative framework that learns interpretable anatomical prototypes from unlabeled medical images. It couples a spatial anatomy prior with a phase-preserving Fourier spectral prior in a dual-domain Gaussian mixture, optimized end-to-end with an alternating EM formulation. Evaluated on OASIS-3 brain MRI, it yields sharper prototypes, cluster separation improvements of up to 94% over spatial-only baselines, and low inference overhead of 0.28 ms per image.

entry.title: The Platonic Brain: Convergence of Representations in EEG Foundation Models
entry.summary: The Platonic Brain: Representational Convergence in EEG Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study tests whether the Platonic Representation Hypothesis applies to human brain representations using EEG foundation models. Recordings from six participants watching a television series, paired with aligned visual and language content, were used to examine whether model representations converge within and across modalities as decoding of EEG markers improves. EEG models with greater decodability showed stronger alignment across model families in both local and global structure, not consistently increasing with parameter count. Cross-modal convergence depended on modality and metric: higher EEG decodability was linked to stronger global alignment with language models, but not consistently with vision models, and local alignment showed no consistent association.

entry.title: LatentTriad: Pre-action risk representations for detecting malicious agent skills
entry.summary: LatentTriad: Pre-Action Risk Representations for Malicious Agent Skill Detection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Large language model agents are increasingly extended with reusable skills, but untrusted skill content can trigger operations beyond the user's task. The authors find that hidden states formed during prefill contain readable information about whether a task and its operations are consistent. They introduce LatentTriad, which combines contextual boundary features, group-adjusted operation directions, and departures from benign state relationships. Detection runs on a single shared prefill without generating output tokens, invoking tools, or executing skill code.

entry.title: Sparse Anchors for Aligning Repeated Robot Recordings in Changing Environments
entry.summary: Sparse Anchors for Visual Multi-Session Registration in Changing Environments arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper addresses aligning a new robot recording of an environment to a previously built reference map, even when the scene has changed. The method gathers absolute pose estimates via place recognition, feature matching and geometric checks, keeps the consistent ones as anchors, and combines them with within-session relative poses in a robust pose-graph optimization. On 15 cross-session experiments from the HILTI26 construction-site dataset, it reaches 94.4% recall within 1 m and 100.0% within 5 m, outperforming independent image localization and direct registration of reconstructed geometry.

entry.title: Image matching method using deep feature manifold embedding and neural adjoint maps
entry.summary: Manifold Embedding of Deep Image Features for Image Matching via Neural Adjoint Maps arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses finding semantic correspondences between different object instances of similar categories in real-world images. It adapts functional maps, used for 3D shape matching, by deriving a discrete Laplace-Beltrami operator from a manifold embedding of deep image features via Galerkin's method, giving image grids a meaningful geometric structure. A neural adjoint map is added to represent non-linear mappings. The authors report state-of-the-art results among zero-shot image correspondence methods on multiple dense correspondence benchmarks.

entry.title: CRONOS: A benchmark for reinforcement learning on robot manipulation without episode resets
entry.summary: CRONOS: Benchmarking Non-Episodic Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces CRONOS, a simulation benchmark for fine-tuning vision-language-action (VLA) robot models with reinforcement learning when scenes are not reset between episodes. The authors find that naively fine-tuning pre-trained policies fails in this setting because of shifts in object configurations and end-effector poses. They report that targeted reset allocation and addressing biases in pre-trained models can mitigate these problems. Non-episodic training is also found to improve long-horizon manipulation and generalization to unseen object configurations and task sequences.

entry.title: Rollout-free world model for scoring self-driving trajectories
entry.summary: Trajectory Evaluation via Rollout-Free World Model for End-to-end Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes RFWorld, a rollout-free world model for evaluating candidate trajectories in end-to-end autonomous driving. Instead of predicting full future scenes for each candidate, it builds a shared scene memory that candidate trajectories query directly through sparse spatial readout. The authors report that this reduces inference cost and avoids accumulated prediction errors, and that it achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive.

entry.title: VIGOR: Visual Gain Ordering to Reduce Hallucination in Diffusion-Based Multimodal Models
entry.summary: VIGOR: Visual Gain Ordering for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Multimodal discrete diffusion language models generate answers by iteratively predicting masked tokens, but they can still hallucinate content that fits language patterns yet lacks support in the image. The paper proposes VIGOR, a training-free, plug-and-play inference method that reorders which masked positions to fill next, based on how much each prediction depends on visual evidence. It compares token confidence with the original image against a pass where the visual input is ablated. The authors report that VIGOR reduces hallucination and improves multimodal reasoning on LLaDA-V and Lumina-DiMOO.

entry.title: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as an Intermediate for Learning Robot Actions from Human Video
entry.summary: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as a World Action Model Intermediate for Learning from Human Video arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents FloMo, a 5B video-generation model fine-tuned to predict 3D scene flow and action tokens. By rendering scene flow as RGB and encoding it in the same latent space as video, a pretrained video backbone adapts efficiently to motion prediction. Co-trained on action-free human video and robot teleoperation data, the model generalizes to unseen objects, motion primitives, and tasks.

entry.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? A Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
entry.summary: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes replacing repeated raw-image reasoning in robot control with a 3D geometric abstraction written as text and symbols. Typed, evidence-aware references to object parts are grounded from calibrated RGB-D data, and after each action the system returns compact textual checkpoints with metric residuals. Across offline policy synthesis and online execution, reasoning over this text and symbolic state improved multi-step manipulation completion while substantially reducing repeated multimodal queries.

entry.title: Ablation study of protein ensemble generator design choices across structural types
entry.summary: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines design choices for generative models of protein conformational ensembles. Using a minimal Cα flow-matching model, the authors ablate architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment and training data source. Variants are evaluated against experimental SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data across ordered, disordered, multi-domain and transitional proteins. The training data, rather than the architecture, is identified as the main constraint.

entry.title: Learning to Recognize Footsteps Across Unseen Footwear
entry.summary: On the Learnability of Footwear Robustness: Footstep Recognition Under Unseen Conditions arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies identifying people from footstep patterns recorded on pressure- or force-sensitive walkways, where enrollment uses one footwear type and recognition uses unseen footwear. The authors propose BiStepNet, which splits spatial and temporal identity cues into two independently trainable streams and outperforms compact 3D spatiotemporal baselines on the StepUP-P150 dataset. Results show cross-footwear performance improves systematically with the volume and diversity of footwear in training, and auxiliary gait datasets with partial modality overlap can further improve robustness.

entry.title: How correlations between emitting partons affect direct-photon yields and elliptic flow in heavy-ion collisions
entry.summary: Effects of Parton Pair Correlations on Direct-Photon Yields and Elliptic Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how correlations between partons that emit photons affect the yield and elliptic flow of direct photons in heavy-ion collisions. The authors show that the local 2→2 photon rate depends on the joint distribution of incoming partons, so a correlation can change photon emission without altering single-particle distributions. Folded over the evolving medium in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions, the correlation raises the photon yield toward fitted PHENIX and ALICE data and increases v2 mainly at intermediate transverse momentum.

entry.title: Positional encoding to relax equivariance constraints during training, more efficiently and scalably
entry.summary: Positional Encoding is All You Need for Scalable Equivariance Constraint Relaxation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper addresses optimization difficulties in strictly equivariant neural networks, which can struggle when data only approximately follow a symmetry. Prior work relaxed equivariance during training with non-equivariant dense layers, but at significant computational cost. The authors propose injecting a positional encoding with learnable scale to break the symmetry, gradually annealing it to zero so the original equivariant model is recovered by the end of training. They report significant gains for translational and rotational equivariant models with only marginal compute and memory overhead.

entry.title: ALBI: LLM-guided inductive logic programming through iterative generate-test-constrain refinement
entry.summary: ALBI: LLM-Guided Inductive Logic Programming via Iterative Generate-Test-Constrain Refineme arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces ALBI, a framework that replaces the ASP-based hypothesis generator in Learning from Failures with a large language model while keeping SWI-Prolog as a formal verifier. It runs an iterative loop in which the LLM proposes candidate hypotheses, Prolog tests them, and diagnostic feedback guides refinement. On 30 standard ILP benchmarks, three frontier LLMs each reached 100% success, matching Popper with about 1.4 to 1.7 iterations on average. Under semantic anonymization, all models still achieved 100% success, with a moderate increase in iterations.

entry.title: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew
entry.summary: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses federated learning on multicentric medical data, which exhibits mixed skew across feature, label, concept, and quantity shifts between centers. It proposes PAFP, a personalized federated learning framework built on a pre-trained backbone that inserts client-specific Feature Alignment modules before fine-tuned blocks to align hidden features toward a server-aggregated target. On the FedISIC benchmark, PAFP achieves the highest unweighted balanced accuracy and reduces inter-client performance variance roughly six-fold relative to the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions
entry.summary: Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper examines activation patching, a method that copies part of a language model's internal state between inputs to locate concepts by measuring output change. The authors prove that, to first order, the effects of orthogonal parts sum to the whole state's effect, so a learned part exceeds the whole only when the remaining components push the output back. Objectives that reward larger output effects select such parts, and changing the objective to target the network's own output removes most of the excess.

entry.title: Comparing representations and fitting methods for learning port-Hamiltonian models
entry.summary: Comparing model representations and fitting methods for port-Hamiltonian system identification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Port-Hamiltonian models describe physical systems by separating stored energy, dissipation and external inputs. The paper compares neural networks, analytic expressions and combinations of the two for representing these components, and compares gradient-based optimisation with sparse regression for fitting. Tests on simulated mechanical and electrical systems, with and without noise, report prediction accuracy and computational cost for each approach.

entry.title: DRAP: A Replay-Free Method for Continual Learning in Physical AI
entry.summary: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies continual learning for physical AI, where small per-step policy errors can accumulate along a trajectory and cause closed-loop task failure. It proposes DRAP, a replay-free method that estimates each adaptable tensor's historical importance from action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk, and uses this to reduce plasticity in components that supported earlier behavior. Applied to a fixed subnetwork of OpenVLA and tested on the LIBERO Spatial, Object, and Goal suites, DRAP is reported to retain previously learned behaviors substantially better than standard AdamW fine-tuning and EWC while still acquiring new suites well.

entry.title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems: Letting Operators Steer Robot Groups at Multiple Scales Through Touch Feedback
entry.summary: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper modifies a global connectivity maintenance algorithm so robots can use measurements from their local frames, taken with sensors that have limited fields of view. This algorithm is combined with three adaptive supervision strategies that let an operator control a single robot, pin constraints on several robots, or act on the group's centroid. These methods keep inter-agent constraints satisfied while giving the user haptic feedback about the system's connectivity state. A user study compared performance with and without haptic feedback across scenarios designed for each control mode.

entry.title: Deep learning for on-phone RGB photo enhancement: Mobile AI 2026 challenge report
entry.summary: RGB Photo Enhancement with Deep Learning on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This report describes the Mobile AI 2026 challenge, which asked participants to design fast models that enhance RGB photos while running on smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. Participants used the DPED dataset of image pairs captured by an old iPhone 3GS and a professional Canon 70D DSLR. Models were timed on Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets, and the top solutions enhanced Full HD images in under 300 milliseconds on both platforms.

entry.title: How finite spectral depth affects early rank selection and bypassing the first gradient-flow saddle in matrix factorization training
entry.summary: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies training dynamics of matrix factorization, a simple model of neural network training, under small initialization. It analyzes continuous-time dynamics that applies a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations to the normalized matrix gradient (Muon). The authors show that the number of iterations can change the rank selected early in training and let trajectories bypass the first nonzero stationary point that gradient flow approaches. Under an additional residual-inertia condition, they prove bypass occurs for all sufficiently large finite depths, give an explicit sufficient threshold, and construct an example where the threshold is four.

entry.title: Revisiting GA2Ms: performance and generalisation to shifted data
entry.summary: Rethinking GA2Ms: performance and out-of-distribution generalisation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines spline-based Generalised Additive Models (GAMs), which are interpretable machine learning models, on large tabular datasets and under distribution shift. The authors propose CoGA2M, a multi-resolution, higher-order composite GAM, and evaluate it on the TALENT benchmark suite, where it ranks in the top third of all baselines. On out-of-distribution splits with train-test distribution shift, CoGA2M outperforms LightGBM, a consistently strong tabular model.

entry.title: Can heatmap explanations flag chest X-ray AI errors at new hospitals? An external validation study
entry.summary: Can saliency maps flag chest radiograph classifier errors at a new hospital? An external validation study arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The study trained a convolutional network and a vision transformer on the NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset and tested them on decisions from the training hospital and two external sites in the USA and Vietnam, using radiologist-consensus labels. It measured whether saliency maps' anatomical enrichment could detect errors beyond the model's own confidence. Grad-CAM localized findings less often than radiologists, and adding enrichment did not meaningfully improve error detection, with its relation to correctness reversing between some hospitals. The authors conclude that model confidence, not saliency, should guide deployment monitoring.

entry.title: Learned Smartphone Image Processing on Mobile GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
entry.summary: Learned Smartphone ISP on Mobile GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This report covers the Mobile AI 2026 challenge, which asked participants to build fast models that turn RAW Bayer camera data into RGB photos on Qualcomm and Arm smartphone GPUs. Participants used a dataset of RAW-RGB image pairs captured with a Sony IMX586 sensor and a FujiFilm GFX100 camera. According to the paper, top solutions reconstructed high-quality 5MP RGB images under 100 milliseconds on both platforms.

entry.title: ScoreDial: precise control of image attributes using a regressor trained on limited human ratings
entry.summary: ScoreDial: Precise Control of Visual Attributes in Image Generation via Regressor Guidance from Limited Human Ratings arXiv · Nov 3, 2026ScoreDial trains a differentiable regressor on 100 to 479 human-rated images so that image generation can reach a requested rating value. Tested on tire slip resistance, interior visual complexity, food desire-to-eat, and soap translucency, it achieves low regression error and high Spearman correlation. Its agreement is also checked with an independent auditor and blinded human judgments.

entry.title: Exact selective testing for spectral clustering results
entry.summary: Exact Selective Inference for Spectral Clustering via Piecewise-Constant Graph Perturbation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper addresses the problem that testing differences between clusters found by the same data is biased. For spectral clustering on unweighted ε- or k-nearest-neighbor graphs, it shows that along the one-dimensional perturbation used by the truncated-χ test, the graph changes only at finitely many real roots of data-dependent quadratic distance comparisons. The selection event is therefore an exact finite union of intervals, yielding finite-sample selective p-values for selected cluster pairs.

entry.title: ProAlign: Progressive Positional and Prototype-Guided Alignment for Matching Pedestrians Across Drone and Ground Cameras
entry.summary: ProAlign: Progressive Positional and Prototype-Guided Alignment for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses aerial-ground person re-identification, the task of matching pedestrians seen by drones and ground cameras. It proposes ProAlign, which includes a layer-wise positional embedding module that uses conditional encoding in shallow layers and learnable static embeddings in deeper layers. A view-aware prototype contrastive module keeps aerial and ground prototypes per identity consistent across views. The authors report state-of-the-art overall retrieval results on CARGO and two real-world benchmarks.

entry.title: GeoFaham: A Multi-Agent System for Disaster Mapping and Geospatial Analysis
entry.summary: GeoFaham: Domain-Specialized Multi-Agent Geospatial Analytics for Disaster Response arXiv · Nov 3, 2026GeoFaham is a multi-agent system built to answer disaster-response questions that require combining spatial databases, map features, satellite imagery, and raster data. Specialist agents handle vector operations, feature retrieval, imagery discovery, and raster analysis, coordinated by an orchestrator that plans, validates, and replans tasks. A Response Store keeps full geospatial outputs outside the model's context while agents share compact identifiers and summaries. On the 40-task GeoFaham-Bench, built from 17 real disaster records, it scored 0.940 against 0.879 for the next-best coding-agent baseline while using 7.5 times fewer tokens.

entry.title: LLMs as Designers of Robot Learning Setups: A Dependency-Aware Framework for Automatic Policy Generation
entry.summary: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies generating executable robot reinforcement learning policies automatically from natural-language task descriptions. The authors use large language models as designers that build the RL pipeline before deployment, including MDP formulation and simulator implementation. They propose ARPG, an agentic framework that models the MDP sequentially, verifies and corrects locally, and implements the simulator in a modular way. Experiments in Isaac Sim report gains in modeling correctness, environment executability, and policy-generation success over monolithic LLM baselines and off-the-shelf agentic systems.

entry.title: Comparing LLMs and humans on judging whether “they” is singular or plural
entry.summary: Who is the Pronoun Pro? Comparing LLMs and Humans at Number-Disambiguation of 'they' arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study compares 73 human annotators with more than 40 large language model configurations on deciding whether 174 real Reddit uses of "they" refer to one or several people. The best model, Kimi K3, reached 94.5% accuracy, above the human majority vote of 86.2%, though only the single best human scored higher. The authors conclude that LLMs are viable for large-scale linguistic annotation but require human oversight, since human reasoning in ambiguous cases exposed inconsistencies in the annotation scheme.

entry.title: An AI agent framework that adapts image compression to different goals and degraded inputs
entry.summary: An Agentic Framework for Quality-Aware and Scenario-Adaptive Image Compression arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes PICA, a multi-agent framework that adapts existing image codecs to diverse user requirements and degraded inputs. It uses four collaborating agents for perception, pre-coding restoration, coding control, and after-coding improvement, along with AROIC for codec-agnostic regional coding and an SGQR evaluation strategy. Experiments on H.266/VVC and Cheng2020 codecs report improved compression performance over competing methods on Kodak, CLIC2020, and HEVC datasets.

entry.title: Lightweight graph transformers for classifying radar clutter and targets in cars
entry.summary: Lightweight graph transformers for clutter and target classification in automotive radar arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes TGTNet, a lightweight tiny graph transformer network that classifies clutter, meaning false detections of non-existent moving objects, from stationary and moving targets in automotive radar scenes. Evaluated on the public RadarScenes dataset, TGTNet reaches precision and recall similar to state-of-the-art models. It has one to two orders of magnitude smaller model size and much faster inference.

entry.title: Shuffled OPSD: Does Keeping Problem Statements Coherent Hurt Self-Distillation?
entry.summary: Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), where one model acts as both teacher and student under different contexts. The authors propose Shuffled OPSD, which shuffles the words of the shared problem statement while keeping the teacher-only worked example intact. Across three math reasoning benchmarks and three Qwen3 model sizes, it improves mean accuracy over standard OPSD, with the largest gain of 3.52 points on Qwen3-1.7B. Shuffling the teacher-only worked example instead reduces accuracy at every scale.

entry.title: Neural network learning of solution maps for stochastic heat equations
entry.summary: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proves a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in spatial dimension d≥2, with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing. A smooth Fourier cutoff reduces the forcing to finitely many measurements, and Besov and Schauder estimates control the solution error. The finite-dimensional solution map is approximated by ReLU branch networks and grid-based trunk functions, with explicit bounds on their numbers. The paper also gives a high-probability local-in-time approximation result for stochastic Navier--Stokes equations.

entry.title: From Artifacts to Capabilities: Diagnosing Failures in Self-Evolving Agents
entry.summary: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how self-evolving agents write interaction experience into artifacts and reuse them later. The authors define capability formation from artifacts as five sequentially dependent properties and propose a three-scale diagnosis at the state, game, and lineage levels. In freestyle Gomoku, Reflexion, Voyager, and DGM, all built on the same base model, each shows the common signals yet breaks in capability formation in a distinct way. The authors conclude that signal-based evaluation cannot determine whether a capability has actually formed.

entry.title: DPAGait: A pose-aware network for gait recognition in real-world settings
entry.summary: DPAGait: Dynamic Pose-Knowledge-Aware Network for Robust Gait Recognition in the Wild arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses gait recognition in unconstrained real-world conditions, where clothing, carried objects, viewpoints, and environments degrade accuracy for existing silhouette-based methods. The authors propose a Dynamic Pose-Parsing enhanced Silhouette (DPPS) representation that combines pose-parsing cues with silhouettes to add information and capture fine-grained motion. They build a dual-branch network with a 2D dynamic pose branch and a 3D SMPL-based branch, whose features are fused for recognition. Experiments on four in-the-wild datasets show the effectiveness and generalizability of DPPS, with competitive results on SUSTech1K, CCPG, and Gait3D.

entry.title: HERIT: Making Hanja-to-English Historical Translation Globally Accessible by Reducing Temporal Bias
entry.summary: HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes HERIT, a domain-adaptation pipeline that uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to create pseudo-labeled training data from abundant Hanja-Korean corpora. The approach expands the training set to reduce both data scarcity and overfitting to particular historical periods. Automated and human evaluations show HERIT consistently outperforms baselines. The authors also use the model to translate previously untranslated parts of historical archives.

entry.title: PATTS: Parallel-aware test-time scaling for joint thought-image generation in multimodal diffusion language models
entry.summary: PATTS: Parallel-Aware Test-Time Scaling for Thought-Image Generation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion LLMs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes PATTS, a framework that searches over intermediate thought-image states during generation in parallel multimodal discrete diffusion language models. It uses cross-modal verifier signals, weighted by a reliability score derived from model-internal trajectory diagnostics. On MMaDA-Parallel with N=32, PATTS achieves a GenEval score of 0.844, versus 0.628 without test-time scaling, 0.787 for Best-of-N, and 0.810 for FKD.

entry.title: How well webcam eye tracking works in real settings: a large-scale test of Chiasm and a comparison with WebGazer
entry.summary: How Well Does Webcam Eye Tracking Work "in the Wild"? A Large-Scale Validation of Chiasm and a Comparison with WebGazer arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The study tested the first-generation Chiasm webcam eye tracker in an online experiment with 505 participants, finding a mean spatial accuracy of 2.39 cm and spatial precision of 1.05 cm. Compared with the open-source tracker WebGazer in an identical protocol with 101 participants each, Chiasm showed better spatial accuracy and spatial precision, while WebGazer had better sample-to-sample precision. The authors conclude that Chiasm is narrowing the gap between webcam and hardware-based eye tracking.

entry.title: Local visibility roadmaps for continuous multi-agent path finding
entry.summary: Local Visibility Roadmaps in Continous Multi-agent Path Finding arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies smooth continuous multi-agent path finding, where agents move through a continuous environment along smooth curves over continuous time. Individual paths are searched within local visibility roadmaps that account for obstacles and other agents. The authors propose an algorithm that combines the high-level search of CE-CBS with any-angle path finding for local single-agent planning. Experiments show advantages over CE-CBS and SMT-CCBS in comparable settings.

entry.title: Learning Where to Look: Optimizing Image Observation Actions for Visual Reasoning
entry.summary: Learning Where to Look: Observation Policy Optimization for Thinking with Images arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies vision-language models that answer complex questions by zooming into regions of high-resolution images. The authors find that many errors come from poor observation actions, such as choosing the wrong crop. They propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), a reinforcement learning method that branches at uncertain zoom-in decisions and gives credit to the specific observation tokens. Experiments report consistent gains for Qwen3-VL models and competitive results against larger models and tool-augmented baselines.

entry.title: HTNN-MSC: Multi-view Clustering with a Bounded Tensor Rank Surrogate
entry.summary: HTNN-MSC: Multi-view Subspace Clustering with a Hyperbolic Tangent Tensor Low-Rank Surrogate arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes HTNN-MSC, a multi-view subspace clustering method that replaces the tensor nuclear norm with a bounded hyperbolic tangent tensor rank surrogate to avoid over-shrinking dominant singular values. The authors develop an ADMM solver and establish convergence of the full sequence to a KKT point under explicit conditions. On 23 datasets it reaches a mean clustering accuracy of 0.8404, outperforming its convex t-SVD-based skeleton in most cases, though it does not uniformly beat other nonconvex penalties.

entry.title: Verifying Neural Network Robustness to Patch Attacks Using Group-Lasso Semidefinite Relaxation
entry.summary: Robustness Verification against Patch Attacks via Group-Lasso Semidefinite Relaxation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Robustness verification of neural networks has mostly addressed norm-ball attacks, which do not capture physical patch attacks. The paper models patch attacks with group-wise sparsity and formulates verification as a mixed-integer semidefinite program, then proposes three relaxations that remove integer variables. The Group-Lasso relaxation keeps the objective within 0.34% on average of the original formulation while using under 3% of its computation time. It achieves a 91% verified rate, compared with under 70% for prior methods.

entry.title: VISTA: A vision-language framework that groups faces by identity in long videos as they stream in.
entry.summary: VISTA: Vision-Language Integrated Semantic Triage Architecture for Online Face Clustering in Long Videos arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces VISTA, described as the first vision-language framework for online face clustering in long videos, which groups faces by identity as the video is processed. Existing online methods based on geometric features and simple thresholding struggle when appearance varies widely, while VISTA uses semantic reasoning in a controlled, uncertainty-aware way. On the VPCD benchmark, the authors report that VISTA achieves a better precision and recall balance than the strongest matched online unsupervised baseline, COFC, under identical detector, embeddings, and evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Adjusting LoRA merge strength in continual learning via joint loss estimation
entry.summary: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses LoRA-based continual learning methods that scale each new task's update with one shared coefficient. It proposes M2LE, which combines Hessian-guided adaptive merging (HIM) and task simulation perturbation (TSP). HIM solves for the merged update under a joint objective over previous and current tasks, yielding element-wise modulation. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show M2LE outperforms existing PEFT-based continual learning methods.

entry.title: PROSE: A Method for Fixing Wrongful Guilty Verdicts in Legal Judgment Prediction Models
entry.summary: PROSE: Preservation-Constrained Selective Editing for Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies "guilty bias," where legal judgment prediction models keep a guilty verdict even after the condition that establishes the charge has been changed. The authors build CAIL-MC, a legally reviewed dataset of 11,478 matched case pairs covering 261 Chinese criminal charges. They propose PROSE, a method that selectively edits the model via a preservation-regularized low-rank update to correct false-guilty decisions while keeping supported-guilty decisions stable.

entry.title: Behind Video Generation: Kling's Insights on Multimodal Understanding
entry.summary: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This report summarizes observations and lessons on multimodal understanding gained across successive generations of Kling, a video generation system. It argues that generation quality reflects multimodal understanding across the data, conditioning, alignment, and evaluation chain, and examines each module. The authors describe Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model handling image, video, and audio inputs, along with designs for captioning, prompt enhancement, reward modeling, and automatic evaluation.

entry.title: EP-LVMQA: Coarse-to-fine localization that preserves evidence for low-quality long-video question answering
entry.summary: EP-LVMQA: Evidence-Preserving Coarse-to-Fine Localization for Low-Quality Long Video Moment Question Answering arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper addresses question answering over long instructional videos whose subtitles, speech transcripts, or on-screen text are missing or noisy, and it requires the system to return timestamped evidence supporting each answer. It proposes EP-LVMQA, a framework with an uncertainty-aware multimodal evidence timeline, a coarse evidence planner, and an evidence-conditioned fine localizer. On MedVidQA it reports higher localization and evidence metrics than the strongest prior non-proposed methods, and smaller performance degradation under low-quality perturbations.

entry.title: MiCaDe: Online Detection of LiDAR-Camera Calibration Drift in Self-Driving Cars
entry.summary: MiCaDe: Online LiDAR-Camera Miscalibration Change Detection for Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents MiCaDe, an online method that detects when the extrinsic calibration between a LiDAR and a camera on an autonomous vehicle has drifted and is no longer accurate. It needs no calibration targets or changes to the perception stack, and it checks whether 3D and 2D detection boxes from both sensors remain geometrically consistent. A change point model accumulates evidence over time to catch subtle drifts. The authors report reliable detection on several long-sequence datasets and on a real-world dataset with physically induced miscalibration.

entry.title: Cool Graphs: active search for quantum nano-refrigerators.
entry.summary: Cool Graphs: Active Property Search Towards Quantum Nano-Refrigerators arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a search framework for finding nanodevice configurations that absorb energy from their thermal surroundings and can act as quantum refrigerators. It combines a Graph Variational Autoencoder with an uncertainty-driven active learning loop to select promising candidates for expensive quantum-chemical simulation. The authors report that this strategy finds energy-absorbing systems faster than random sampling across all tested topologies.

entry.title: Heads That Write, Not Just Point: Attention Heads for Image Retrieval in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: Heads That Write, Not Just Point: Image Retrieval Heads in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how large vision-language models identify the image relevant to a question when several images appear in one context. It introduces ICIR-MCQ, a controlled probe for analyzing individual attention heads, and finds sparse pointer heads that reliably point to the target image, with one head competitive with external retrievers. An output-side analysis identifies writer heads whose outputs carry enough information to identify the target, and the two head sets overlap only slightly. Heads selected by both criteria show the most consistent causal effects.

entry.title: Attention on Recurrent Memory Writes Reduces Seed Variance in Length Generalization
entry.summary: Attending to Memory Writes Reduces Seed Variability in Recurrent Length Generalization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies bounded delta attention, which applies causal attention to uncorrected update proposals and adds a bounded correction to the recurrent update. On a prefix-supervised modulo-5 task trained on lengths 1 to 40 and tested at length 80, it reports a 63.2% lower standard deviation across seven seeds than a local-attention recurrent baseline, with similar mean accuracy. The authors present bounded update-level attention as a scaffold for recurrent learning that reduces seed variation and extrapolation degradation.

entry.title: VisSearch-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Visual Search by AI Agents
entry.summary: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents arXiv · Nov 3, 2026VisSearch-Bench is a benchmark of 204 human-written tasks across 7 main domains and 25 subdomains, designed to test how multimodal agents organize visual information and link it to search results. Each task includes a reference answer, traceable evidence, and scoring rules, with accuracy and Process Score used as metrics. Across 16 multimodal models, the best system fully solved only 26.47% of tasks, even with search tools.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant sparse sensing for state estimation with missing sensor data
entry.summary: Fault-tolerant shallow recurrent decoders for sparse sensing with missing sensor measurements arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses sensing systems whose sensors may fail, disconnect, or sample asynchronously, producing incomplete measurement streams. The authors extend shallow recurrent decoders (SHRED) with four transformer-based masking mechanisms that make the model aware of which sensors are available, and add a multi-step decoding training objective. On a synthetic benchmark and three real-world hydrodynamic and ocean modeling problems, the transformer-based masking outperforms standard imputation and fault-tolerant recurrent architectures, and the multi-step objective improves fidelity and robustness. The method keeps SHRED's computational efficiency, with no added inference-time overhead.

entry.title: FourSight: Stable 4-bit Reinforcement Learning Training via Sequence Filtering and Sparse Compensation
entry.summary: FourSight: Stable FP4 RL Post-Training via Sequence Filtering and Sparse Channel Compensation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses problems that arise when reinforcement learning post-training uses NVFP4 4-bit quantization, including degraded rollout quality and mismatch between training and inference engines. The proposed FourSight method filters out sequences whose behavior has drifted too far from the reference, and keeps only the highest-variance activation channels in BF16 while leaving the rest in NVFP4. A fused kernel is also designed to reduce overhead.

entry.title: Modelling how AI adoption can lock in through skill erosion
entry.summary: Modelling lock-in of AI adoption through skill erosion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper builds a model in which individuals imitate successful peers, while independent skills grow with practice and erode with reliance on AI. It finds that skill erosion can produce bistability and hysteresis between a low-adoption, high-skill state and a high-adoption, low-skill state, with asymmetric transitions. The authors argue that this history-dependent switching cost can make widespread AI adoption difficult to reverse.

entry.title: DLER: Dual-Logit Experience Replay for Online Continual Learning
entry.summary: DLER: Dual-Logit Experience Replay for Online Continual Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes Dual-Logit Experience Replay (DLER), a method for online continual learning that aims to reduce forgetting and bias toward current classes when neural networks learn from a non-stationary data stream. It splits dot-product logits into angle and norm factors, using cosine logits for current samples and adding dot-product logits when replaying past samples. An auxiliary supervised contrastive objective and a memory update strategy based on dual-logit predictions are also introduced. Experiments on three datasets show its effectiveness, especially under limited memory budgets.

entry.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Testing Web Agents Against Online Scams
entry.summary: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces ScamWorld, an interactive environment that recreates reported scam websites across various scenarios, fraud methods, and languages to allow controlled, repeatable testing of web agents. Studying web agents powered by six frontier LLMs, the authors find baseline deception rates between 11% and 35%. Agents are more willing to proceed with payments than with requests for credentials or wallet information. Some agents recognized suspicious conditions but continued anyway, sometimes treating user instructions as approval to accept extra terms imposed by the website.

entry.title: TraceRouter++: A Safety Method That Redirects Harmful Signal Routes in AI Models Using Optimal Transport
entry.summary: TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large foundation models can still be manipulated by adversarial inputs, and existing safety methods that suppress isolated neurons are brittle and can hurt general performance. TraceRouter++ is a framework that finds safety-relevant causal routing pathways activated by harmful inputs and realigns their unsafe activations. It uses attention divergence, sparse autoencoders, and feature influence scores to locate and trace these pathways, then applies a constrained optimal transport method to steer unsafe activations toward safe reference distributions. Experiments on language, multimodal, and diffusion models report improved adversarial robustness and a favorable safety-utility trade-off.

entry.title: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: Shifting From Specialist to Unified Models
entry.summary: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: From Specialist Models to Unified Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This survey reviews the development of optical character recognition (OCR), focusing on the shift from specialist models to unified models in the foundation model era. It examines joint text detection and recognition, structured sequence generation, and the use of pretrained vision-language models. The paper organizes contemporary OCR systems into five families and discusses issues such as hallucination, omission, weak spatial grounding, and inference cost. It also reviews evaluation practices and outlines open challenges and future research directions.

entry.title: Trusting Imagined Futures: Checking Imagined Rewards to Guide Robot Action Model Training
entry.summary: Trusting Imagined Futures: Auditing Imagined Rewards for VLA Post-Training arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes TIF, an offline method for choosing training data for vision-language-action robot models. It uses execution feedback to audit rewards predicted by video world models, adopting a candidate trajectory only when its predicted advantage and audit risk meet set thresholds, and otherwise keeping the existing real trajectories. Across four LIBERO suites, TIF reaches a mean success rate of 76.25%, 3.00 percentage points above training on the existing trajectories. On recorded videos from three real robot tasks, clean completion among selected trajectories rises from 58.33% to 70.00%.

entry.title: One Assistant, Many Memories: A Real-World Benchmark for Group Chat Assistance
entry.summary: One Assistant, Many Memories: Benchmarking Real-World Group Assistance When Recall Is Not Enough arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces GroupAssistBench, the first memory benchmark built from real group conversations with a deployed group assistant, covering 80,299 messages across 50 groups. It evaluates both memory recall and memory use, the latter with service requests that have no fixed answers, across single, distributed, and conflicting memories. The results show that the strongest memory system matches full-context methods on recall but falls far behind on use, especially for distributed and conflicting memories.

entry.title: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection Using Prior-Data Fitted Networks
entry.summary: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection with Prior-Data Fitted Networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes MambaPFN, a model-agnostic method for selecting variables that have general nonlinear dependence on a response, built on the Transformer architecture. It combines a pretraining data generation scheme, an objective targeting each variable's posterior inclusion probability, and a Transformer tailored for variable selection. Once pretrained, it applies to new datasets without parameter updates. In simulations it performs well and shows performance gains as pretraining data and model size grow, and on a Facebook comments dataset it selects the fewest variables with the highest efficiency and predictive performance, about 20% better than the best baselines.

entry.title: DGC-Net: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Network with Cross-Modal Routing and Global Compensation
entry.summary: DGC-Net: Cross-Modal Dynamic Routing with Global-Guided Compensation in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes DGC-Net, a network for multimodal sentiment analysis that combines text, voice, and facial cues to judge a speaker's attitude in videos. It uses cross-modal dynamic expert routing, guided by global context, to reduce inconsistency among affective cues from different modalities. A global-guided dynamic compensation fusion balances global semantics with adaptively selected local cues. The authors report that experiments on five multimodal benchmark datasets demonstrate its effectiveness and general applicability.

entry.title: Intrinsic rewards found by search, then broken by a shortcut
entry.summary: Found by Search, Broken by a Shortcut: Transfer and Tampering of Searched Intrinsic Rewards arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper searches for intrinsic rewards built from four generic events (new view, pickup, drop, toggle) to see whether they help reinforcement-learning agents learn and transfer to unseen tasks. On the held-out KeyCorridorS3R2 task, the CMA-ES-selected reward beat task-only PPO, episodic novelty, and a random-search-selected reward. On the training tasks, it showed no registered advantage over the random-search reward, and a free reset action absent during search collapsed its learning on DoorKey-8x8.

entry.title: HTCE: A topology-based method for canonicalizing and reusing navigation experience across scenes for object-goal navigation
entry.summary: HTCE: Homeomorphism-inspired Topological Cross-Scene Experience Canonicalization and Reuse for Object Navigation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces HTCE, a framework that organizes successful navigation experiences of embodied agents into canonical topological representations. It keeps semantic anchors, branching relations, and endpoints while reducing differences in region naming and observation granularity. Retrieved past successful routes guide a frozen vision-language policy. Canonicalization losslessly compresses the experience index, merging 17.7 to 23.6 percent of stored route descriptions, and the method reports its best success rate and SPL on HM3D and MP3D benchmarks.

entry.title: Anomaly detection on tiny devices using reservoir computing
entry.summary: Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained Devices with Reservoir Computing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether the MDRS method, an unsupervised time-series anomaly detector, suits resource-constrained devices, and proposes two optimizations to cut its computation. Random reservoir connectivity is replaced with a circular shift, and the reservoir's temporal memory enables cheaper input preprocessing. On the MLPerf Tiny anomaly detection benchmark, optimized MDRS reaches an ROC AUC of 0.869 with a 24 KB model, a 75.9x speedup over the autoencoder with standard preprocessing.

entry.title: Feeling of Knowing in LLMs: How Models Judge Whether They Can Answer
entry.summary: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how post-training updates can leave a large language model's judgment of what it can answer out of step with what it actually knows. It defines a functional feeling of knowing (FoK) that supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing, without implying subjective experience. The authors propose a knowledge channel and a FoK channel, trained in three stages: on-policy supervised fine-tuning, knowledge-delta FoK training, and FoK-guided policy optimization. Factual-QA experiments reportedly show that explicit FoK alignment improves judgment quality on updated knowledge, with MMLU and ARC-Easy used to check capability preservation.

entry.title: UniFlow: A Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching Method for Generating Time Series
entry.summary: UniFlow: Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching for Time Series Generation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes UniFlow, a framework that combines multi-scale time series representation learning with non-autoregressive generation. Its multi-scale tokenizer uses shared-index voting to merge temporal information from different scales into a single public-ID sequence, while scale-specific codebooks retain what is needed for reconstruction. The authors also introduce geometry-aware categorical flow matching and run experiments on four benchmarks covering short- and long-term settings.

entry.title: Estimating homography with radial distortion using affine- or orientation-covariant features
entry.summary: Radial distortion homography estimation from affine-covariant or orientation-covariant features arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents minimal solvers that jointly estimate homography and radial distortion using the local geometry of affine or orientation-covariant features. The solvers need fewer correspondences than point-based methods. Built on modern robust estimation frameworks, they run significantly faster in the presence of outliers while keeping accuracy comparable to or better than the current state of the art. The solvers are tested on synthetic and real images with fisheye distortion.

entry.title: Interpretable Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Reconstructing Online Payment Fraud Strategies
entry.summary: Reconstructing Fraudulent Strategies in Online Payments via Interpretable Inverse Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes PaySeqGen, an interpretable inverse reinforcement learning framework that reconstructs fraudsters' behavior policies from observed payment trajectories. The framework generates new fraud sequences to augment fraud detectors and learns interpretable rewards that support analysis of fraud patterns in real trajectories. Experiments at Ant International show it outperforms state-of-the-art generative augmentation methods.

entry.title: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Pixel: Text-Based Unlearnable Examples for Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: The Pen is Mightier than the Pixel: Natural Textual Unlearnable Example for Large Vision Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes Natural Textual Unlearnable Examples (NTUE), a data protection method that subtly alters image labels to mislead Large Vision Language Models during training. The approach creates a shortcut between an identity of interest and a separate target without adding factual misinformation or hurting readability. Experiments against traditional unlearnable example methods show NTUE performs better, reaching a high success rate with a poison rate as low as 5%.

entry.title: Think Less, Locally: Local preference learning to compress reasoning
entry.summary: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large reasoning models often keep deliberating after they already have enough information, which raises inference cost. LoCo detects overthinking states in the model's own traces, freezes the reasoning prefix, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same state, and trains on these state-conditioned preference pairs with DPO. Evaluated on five math and three code benchmarks, it cuts completion length by 41.7%–45.4% on math and 23.4%–36.3% on code while maintaining or improving accuracy.

entry.title: AgenticFinBench: A Benchmark Testing AI Finance Agents on Varied Real-World Tasks
entry.summary: AgenticFinBench: Benchmarking Financial Agents on Diverse Tasks from Real-World Requests arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces AgenticFinBench, a benchmark of 230 real-world financial tasks across 8 categories, 2 languages, and 4 complexity levels. It proposes a reference-free evaluation framework that combines question-specific rubrics with a two-stage claim audit to detect hallucinations. Experiments on 18 agent configurations show that ignoring hallucinations overstates performance, and that harness differences affect evidence grounding more than model differences.

entry.title: NightIQA: A dataset and benchmark for evaluating nighttime image quality with multimodal AI models
entry.summary: NightIQA: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for MLLM-Based Nighttime Image Quality Assessment arXiv · Nov 3, 2026NightIQA introduces a real-world nighttime image dataset of 1,769 images, a benchmark of 1,078 multiple-choice questions, and a scalable synthesis pipeline with an initial release of 80k images. The authors fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B using Supervised Fine-Tuning and Group Relative Policy Optimization. The fine-tuned model outperforms open-source image quality assessment methods and achieves higher overall accuracy than some leading closed-source models.

entry.title: RAHC: Rule-augmented knowledge graph completion for filling in missing materials synthesis conditions
entry.summary: RAHC: Rule-Augmented Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graph Completion for Materials Synthesis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes RAHC, a framework that completes missing synthesis conditions in materials experiment records using a hyper-relational knowledge graph. It builds traceable rules from training records and retrieved literature, applying hard rules to constrain candidates and soft rules to rank them. Experiments on five materials-synthesis datasets show improved single-slot and joint completion, with Semi-inductive MRR gains of up to 15.6% over MAYPL.

entry.title: Asymptotic optimality of the cμ rule for LLM inference scheduling under memory limits
entry.summary: Asymptotic Optimality of cμ-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to schedule online requests for large language model inference, where requests with varying prompt and output lengths compete for limited key-value cache memory. The authors build a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue, yielding a cμ priority rule whose effective service rate depends on computation speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. They prove the rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for finite workloads, minimizes completion time and maximizes output-token throughput. Experiments on an NVIDIA H800 serving engine indicate that practical versions of the rule substantially reduce average latency while keeping throughput high compared with existing policies.

entry.title: When AI agents disagree, where is the truth? Dependence-aware belief propagation for label-free truth discovery (extended version)
entry.summary: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version) arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large language model agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents share a base model, so their errors are correlated. The paper proposes BP-TD, a label-free method that infers the true answer and each agent's reliability by adding decorrelation weights so that agents sharing a base model count together as roughly one vote. On MMLU, BP-TD outperforms majority vote, but its benefit depends on the composition of the agent pool, and the authors found no label-free statistic that distinguishes when it helps. With a small number of labelled questions, selecting the single best agent outperformed all aggregators tested.

entry.title: Training Phone-Based Specialist LLMs Using Forward-Only Optimization
entry.summary: Training Specialist LLMs on Your Phone: Forward-Only Optimization via Block-Spectral Coordinates arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents MobileSpec, a system that trains lightweight specialist versions of on-device language models using only forward passes, learning from automatically checked task outcomes. Its core algorithm, FuRA-S, trains only the singular values of column blocks of pretrained weights, yielding specialists of 1-5 MB that update 0.015-0.05% of parameters. The authors report that success rates of a phone-use agent rise from 6-23% to 89-100%, and that a personalized 8B model can be trained overnight on an iPhone 16 Pro.

entry.title: Speeding Up Offloading-Based MoE Inference by Interleaving Concurrent Requests
entry.summary: Accelerating Offloading-Based MoE Inference by Interleaving Concurrent Requests arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses running large mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models locally using expert offloading, where missing experts are fetched during inference. The authors find that prefetching can hurt performance when a GPU expert cache exists, because predictions become less accurate and waste bandwidth and memory. They present Bevy, which lets requests with available experts run ahead to reveal needed experts and overlaps fetching with computation of ready requests, without predicting expert selection. On two local platforms, Bevy achieves up to 3.46 times the decode throughput of llama.cpp and up to 1.55 times that of the fastest prefetching baseline.

entry.title: Density-Aware Reward Scaling: an RL method for sampling in proportion to reward
