entry.summary: Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Density-Aware Reward Scaling (DARS), a reward-processing step for reinforcement learning that scales each reward inversely by the local density of outcomes within an on-policy rollout group. It works with standard policy-gradient training and needs no learned density model or critic. In a multimodal navigation task, DARS-GRPO avoids the single-mode collapse seen with GRPO, and in text-to-image prompt adaptation it improves image and prompt diversity while keeping semantic alignment.

entry.title: ReSI-Math: Recovering Hidden Reasoning Ability for Efficient Math Training
entry.summary: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper argues that when a language model fails a math problem, it may still possess the needed ability, which can be recovered by searching its own reasoning trajectories. The authors define a policy-dependent "recoverable capability frontier" and propose ReSI-Math, which uses self-judge-guided evolutionary search to find such problems and selects them for sequential reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. On Qwen3-VL-8B, trajectory crossover yielded 272 verified correct offspring from 621 attempts, and after three stages the MATH500 and WE-MATH average rose from 78.71 to 80.16.

entry.title: Kierston and KierstonBench: A Simulated Allentown, PA Testbed for Evaluating Language Models in Crime Investigation
entry.summary: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents Kierston, a city-scale simulation of about 125,000 Allentown, Pennsylvania residents that generates telecommunications, financial, administrative, and license-plate records, and KierstonBench, a benchmark of 32 task families for record linkage and incident investigation. In an evaluation of sixteen language models, most could not carry out records investigation and submitted identifications the records did not support. A few frontier models solved most tasks and abstained when evidence was insufficient, yet still fell for common deceptions, and none replaced an investigator.

entry.title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification
entry.summary: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Single-pixel imaging probes an object with known illumination patterns, and a detector without spatial resolution returns one value per pattern, so each measurement costs time and photons. The authors propose LIPS-PC, which learns a fixed linear measurement operator end-to-end with a classification loss, without image reconstruction. Evaluated on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and the industrial X-ray weld dataset RIAWELC, the learned patterns outperform the best fixed transform when measurements are scarce.

entry.title: Replica-Aware Split Inference for Edge IoT Systems
entry.summary: Replica-Aware Split Inference for Edge IoT Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses fault tolerance in split inference, where TinyML model segments are distributed across IoT devices and a device failure can interrupt the pipeline. The authors propose deploying replicas of segments from failed devices onto surviving devices, formulating the selection of replica hosts and communication protocols as a mixed-integer linear programming problem that minimizes post-reconfiguration latency under memory constraints. Simulations with MobileNetV2 on heterogeneous networks and an implementation on 15 IoT devices compare it with four baselines. The method achieves modeled end-to-end inference latency 6.8% lower than Computation Greedy and 18.3% lower than Random on average.

entry.title: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with submodular trajectory rewards
entry.summary: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Submodular Trajectory Rewards arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning where agents have decoupled dynamics and the joint trajectory reward is a monotone submodular function. Because the reward is non-additive, optimal policies can depend on all agents' histories, making exact optimization exponential. The authors introduce pre-window curvature and propose a greedy algorithm that optimizes each agent's local policy sequentially, with an approximation guarantee for fixed window size and polynomial computation time. The method is evaluated on a multi-agent traffic monitoring example.

entry.title: TactiNavi: An LLM Game Coach Serving Strategies with Explicit Conditions
entry.summary: TactiNavi: Serving and Revising an LLM Game Coach with Explicit Strategy Conditions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper describes TactiNavi, the serving system behind an LLM coach in a commercial open-world game. It treats strategy applicability as an explicit artifact shared across offline compilation, online execution, failure diagnosis, and release. In a retrospective evaluation of 1,122 logged coaching turns, condition-bearing strategy packages raised correctness from 57.9% to 82.0% and reduced misapplication under changed player state from 18.1% to 10.4%.

entry.title: Video generation directly in pixel space using U-JiT, a UNet-style transformer
entry.summary: Pixel-space video generation with U-JiT arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines generating videos directly in pixel space, avoiding the two-stage training and information loss that come with latent diffusion models built on pretrained autoencoders. The authors propose a UNet-like transformer architecture (U-JiT) along with changes to the training recipe and sampling strategy. On Kinetics-600 at 128 resolution for frames-to-video, U-JiT improves generative FVD by 27% over prior state-of-the-art and by 14% over the JiT pixel-space baseline.

entry.title: Koopman generative operators for fast probabilistic time-series forecasting
entry.summary: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces the Koopman Generative Operator (KGO), a probabilistic method that treats forecasting as the evolution of structured uncertainty. It combines Koopman patch embedding, Koopman flow matching that generates samples in a single step via a closed-form matrix exponential in latent space, and an adaptive uncertainty gate. The authors report state-of-the-art accuracy on most ProbTS benchmarks and at least a 25 times reduction in inference time compared with iterative generative models.

entry.title: Beyond Local Refinement: Precise Ground-to-Aerial Localization Over Wide Areas
entry.summary: Beyond Local Refinement: Wide-Area Precise Cross-View Localization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies fine-grained cross-view localization, which pinpoints a ground camera within large geo-referenced aerial regions rather than narrow ones. The authors propose RingMatch, a search-and-verification framework that uses predictive uncertainty to find candidate locations and progressively zooms in to gather finer evidence. It adds a depth ring geometric representation and an LVLM verifier to resolve remaining ambiguity. The authors also build VIGOR-Pro, a benchmark composed of contiguous VIGOR aerial tiles spanning up to 400 m, on which RingMatch outperforms representative end-to-end and retrieval-based methods.

entry.title: When Should an LLM Steering Edit Depend on the Input?
entry.summary: When Should an LLM Steering Edit Depend on the Input? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies whether activation steering edits to a language model should depend on the input. It argues that input dependence is needed exactly when the target state varies within the class a query requests, which can be measured before fitting any rule. The authors compare fixed-direction steering with per-query retrieval of nearby stored states, and report that input-dependent steering outperforms fixed steering when targets vary within the class.

entry.title: Non-interfering asymmetric AdamW updates for exploring equifinal internal partitions in hybrid models
entry.summary: Non-Interfering Asymmetric AdamW Updates for Constrained Exploration of Equifinality in Hybrid Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies equifinality in hybrid models, where neural networks supply unresolved parameters of a process-based simulator fitted only to aggregate observations. Using evapotranspiration as the example, the total flux is observed but its split into transpiration and evaporation is not, and random-seed ensembles cover only a narrow range of such splits. The authors propose Non-interfering Asymmetric Network Optimization (NANO), which trains members under an auxiliary repulsion on transpiration without degrading the fit to observations.

entry.title: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception
entry.summary: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces iMED, the first synchronized multi-endoscope dataset for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery, with 340 sequences of about 170K timepoints captured from two independent stereo endoscopes. It spans 14 specimens across ex vivo, postmortem, and live settings. Using a train-on-one, test-on-another protocol, the authors benchmark 23 methods, finding that photometric-only approaches degrade while geometrically regularized methods are more robust.

entry.title: Bounded AUKS: a new metric for anomaly detection based on the bounded area under the Kolmogorov–Smirnov curve
entry.summary: Bounded AUKS: A Novel Evaluation Metric for Anomaly Detection via Bounded Area Under the Kolmogorov--Smirnov Curve arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper notes that widely used metrics such as AUROC and AUPRO approach 100% on datasets like MVTec AD and VisA, which can falsely suggest pixel-level anomaly detection is solved, and that they do not reflect threshold selection. The authors propose Bounded AUKS, which integrates the difference between true and false positive rates within a data-driven range determined by normal test samples to measure how well normal and anomalous score distributions separate. Experiments on 9 models across MVTec AD and VisA indicate that it addresses limitations of existing metrics and better evaluates unsupervised anomaly detection models.

entry.title: TAPES: Task-aligned joint pretraining for transaction event sequences
entry.summary: TAPES: Task-Aligned Joint Predictive Pretraining for Transaction Event Sequences arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes TAPES, a pretraining framework for transaction event sequences. It selects a prediction target set from candidate sets based on the downstream usefulness of representations learned in short joint pretraining trials, then pretrains the encoder with a joint likelihood tied to a shared discrete latent variable before supervised adaptation. Experiments on a real-world transaction-risk setting and multiple public financial benchmarks show TAPES outperforms representative baselines, and ablations validate the target selection and joint modeling components.

entry.title: TEXMET: A Deep Learning Benchmark for Archaeological Textile Reconstruction
entry.summary: TEXMET: A Deep Learning Benchmark for Archaeological Textile Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces TEXMET, a dataset of 18,644 historical textile images from the Metropolitan Museum of Art's Open Access collection, serving as the first textile-specific benchmark for puzzle-solving research. The authors evaluate three puzzle-solving models, JPDVT, FCViT, and DiffAssemble, finding that models pre-trained on standard datasets generalize poorly to textiles while domain-specific fine-tuning is highly effective. The fine-tuned DiffAssemble reaches 85.89% puzzle accuracy on textile data and raises accuracy on 45 degraded Oseberg ship burial fragments from 26.67% to 64.44%.

entry.title: SPOD: Recovering suppressed temporal cues in video AI through single-pass decomposition
entry.summary: SPOD: Recovering Suppressed Temporal Evidence in Video-LLMs via Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses temporal hallucination in Video Large Language Models during time-sensitive tasks such as scene transitions and event ordering. It proposes SPOD, a training-free method that, in one forward pass, identifies salient frames from middle-layer hidden states and splits final hidden states into temporal, prior, and residual components, rescaling each. Experiments on VidHalluc, EventHallusion, and VideoMMMU show it outperforms strong inference-time baselines while keeping near-standard inference efficiency.

entry.title: VISAGE: Per-vertex diffusion method for generating surface appearance on arbitrary 3D heads
entry.summary: VISAGE: Vertex-based Intrinsic Surface Appearance GEneration via Dual-Stream Diffusion for Arbitrary 3D Heads arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents VISAGE, a diffusion-based framework that generates per-vertex albedo and roughness directly on arbitrary 3D head mesh topologies without requiring UV parameterisation. It combines global spectral processing with local geodesic K-nearest-neighbour refinement and conditions on multi-view RGB images through visibility-aware cross-attention. The authors report FID reductions relative to the strongest baseline of 42.7% on NPHM and 22.5% and 4.4% on zero-shot FaceVerse and i3DMM, respectively.

entry.title: Cycle WAM: a robot world model linking actions and video via cycle consistency
entry.summary: Cycle WAM: Coupling Action and Video through Cycle Consistency arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes Cycle WAM, a world action model that treats video and robot actions as paired modalities linked causally. It adds bidirectional conversion to video-action co-training and a differentiable cycle-reconstruction objective to couple forward and inverse dynamics. The authors report state-of-the-art results among comparable methods on LIBERO-Pro and substantial gains over DreamZero on DROID.

entry.title: DenseTwins: A self-supervised method that learns dense multimodal features by separating shared and modality-specific information
entry.summary: DenseTwins: Dense Modality Decoupling for Multimodal Self-Supervision arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes DenseTwins, a self-supervised framework for learning dense, spatially structured representations from multimodal data. It splits the dense feature space into shared and modality-specific components, training with dense cross-modal correspondences and redundancy-reduction objectives. The authors report state-of-the-art or competitive results across multiple multimodal benchmarks and sensing setups.

entry.title: Learning General Oral Image Analysis from Unlabeled Photographs
entry.summary: Learning from Unlabeled Photographs for General Oral Image Analysis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces DOVE (Dental Optical Visual Encoder), a model pretrained with self-supervised learning on about 530,000 unlabeled oral photographs from publicly accessible sources. It is benchmarked against three baselines across five classification and four segmentation datasets. The authors report that DOVE performs best overall in few-shot transfer and label efficiency, and conclude it is a generalizable, label-efficient backbone for oral vision research.

entry.title: CLARA: A framework that asks follow-up questions to clarify vague requests
entry.summary: CLARA: A Cognitively-Driven Clarification Framework for Grounding Ambiguous Requests arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents CLARA, a framework that lets robots or AI systems ask users targeted questions when given vague instructions like "organize the desk," gathering key preferences and object arrangements. The clarified details are turned into structured instructions, which guide a diffusion-based image generator to render the intended final scene for user confirmation. Experiments and user studies report that CLARA produces more accurate and consistent results than another state-of-the-art vision-language model system.

entry.title: One-shot distributed learning that combines worker models with server data using weighted averaging
entry.summary: One-shot Distributed Learning via Weighted Averaging with Server-side Information arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies one-shot distributed learning, where workers fit local models and send them to a server that aggregates them. It analyzes when deterministic nonnegative weighted averaging, including the server's own estimator, can reach the mean squared error order of pooled-data empirical risk minimization. The authors compare sample-size weighting with server-only estimation, supported by analytical examples, synthetic experiments, and CIFAR-10 results with linear and nonlinear classifiers.

entry.title: When ground truth isn't: automatic labels for hallucination detection
entry.summary: When Ground Truth Is Not Ground Truth: Automatic Labeling for Hallucination Detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how hallucination detectors for large language models are evaluated, focusing on automatic labeling that compares model outputs with reference answers using similarity metrics such as BLEURT. Experiments with 15 automatic supervision judges and seven detection baselines show that detector performance varies substantially depending on the chosen judge. Human validation finds that QGen-9B has the lowest misclassification rate (12.86%), while BLEURT and BLEURT-n show rates of 47.23% and 47.32%.

entry.title: Surrogate models for simulating stochastic Al-Cu alloy solidification using a diffusion-based approach.
entry.summary: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces a variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge model (VP-DDBM) that predicts two-dimensional Al-Cu solidification from the current phase, concentration, and temperature fields, applied autoregressively. On two held-out thermal gradients, it yields lower long-horizon errors than deterministic U-Net and SI-ConvNeXt baselines and retains fine dendritic structure over long rollouts. The model predicts phase and concentration evolution about 73 times faster than the phase-field solver.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware prototype learning for adapting models to mixed known and unknown test data
entry.summary: Uncertainty-Aware Prototype Learning for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes UAPA, a plug-and-play method for open-set test-time adaptation, where a source-trained model must adapt to unlabeled test data mixing covariate-shifted known-class and unknown-class samples. It combines uncertainty-driven separation of known and unknown samples, dynamic refinement of class prototypes, and contrastive prototype entropy adaptation. The authors report that UAPA improves average OSCR over the strongest baselines by 2.08 points on CIFAR benchmarks and 1.28 points on Tiny-ImageNet-C.

entry.title: CardioVascBench: A benchmark for ranked diagnosis generation from real Chinese cardiovascular records
entry.summary: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark built from 3,262 de-identified Chinese cardiovascular inpatient cases, linking clinical narratives and ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses coded in ICD-10. Evaluation of 36 systems finds that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily mean higher list precision against discharge references. The authors also present CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline, which in their staged comparison achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone.

entry.title: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A large structured dataset built from MIMIC-IV discharge summaries.
entry.summary: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper releases MIMIC-Note-Extract (MNE), which converts 16 sections of 300,720 free-text discharge summaries from MIMIC-IV into structured tables. It combines deterministic parsing with schema-guided large language model generation. Medical doctor validation reports extraction accuracy above 92% across sections. The authors also use MNE to build a clinical decision-making benchmark for LLM agents.

entry.title: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library Implementing Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing
entry.summary: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library for Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Standard graph neural networks assume neighboring nodes share one feature space, which can cause oversmoothing and weak performance on heterophilic graphs. Sheaf neural networks give each node and edge its own vector space and learn restriction maps between them. The paper introduces Sheaf-MPNN, a PyTorch Geometric library that computes sheaf diffusion through local message passing instead of building a global Laplacian matrix. It implements fifteen families of these networks under one framework, along with a benchmarking suite and a proof of theoretical equivalence to the original formulations.

entry.title: FedCSGA: Genetic-algorithm-based client selection for federated learning
entry.summary: FedCSGA: Client Selection Based on Genetic Algorithm for Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes FedCSGA, which uses a genetic algorithm to select which clients take part in each communication round of federated learning. The selection is scored by a fitness function that combines resource-aware metrics with history-aware participation weighting. Experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet show it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, with accuracy gains of up to 7.0% and faster convergence using fewer communication rounds.

entry.title: Phase-DGS: Phase-guided dynamic Gaussian splatting for unsynchronized multi-view video reconstruction
entry.summary: Phase-DGS: Phase-guided Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from Unsynchronized Multi-view Video arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes Phase-DGS, which replaces conventional timestamps with a semantic phase that describes each frame's state within a motion cycle. Frames showing the same motion state share a phase regardless of camera or capture time, allowing correspondence across unsynchronized cameras. The method is tested under temporal offsets, frame drops, and camera freezes, reporting up to +8.5 dB PSNR over baselines. It also integrates with existing dynamic Gaussian splatting backbones such as RealTime-4DGS and FreeTimeGS.

entry.title: Comparing feature-based machine learning and deep learning for classifying variable stars from light curves.
entry.summary: Feature-Based and Deep Learning Methods for Astronomical Light Curve Classification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper compares traditional feature-based machine learning with end-to-end deep learning for classifying variable stars, using the ZTF StarEmbed dataset of about 40,000 objects across seven imbalanced classes. Classical models trained on physically motivated features consistently outperform deep networks trained on raw light curves. The authors attribute the gap partly to limited labeled data and to the multivariate, irregularly sampled, and morphologically diverse nature of light curves.

entry.title: Best-of-Depth: training looped Transformers to explore solutions across depths
entry.summary: Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces Best-of-Depth (BoD), a training objective that treats a looped Transformer's recurrent trajectory as a set of candidate solutions by minimizing prediction loss across depths, without architectural changes or depth-specific labels. On N-Queens completion and graph coloring, BoD improves solution coverage over final-depth and intermediate-supervision training, reaching 91.03% on N-Queens versus 45.75% for final-depth training.

entry.title: Leakage-free evaluation of residual graph convolutional networks for intrusion detection
entry.summary: Leakage-free evaluation of residual graph convolutional networks for network intrusion detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper evaluates residual graph convolutional networks, a type of graph neural network, for network intrusion detection. After removing data leakage and duplicate flows between training and test sets, the authors compare the model with several baselines. Under this protocol, graph message passing gives no measurable accuracy gain over a multilayer perceptron without a graph, and tree ensembles perform stronger. The graph models' advantage lies in robustness to feature noise.

entry.title: Using Attention Biases to Cut Transformer Computation Cost
entry.summary: Exploiting Biases in Attention for Transformers arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper finds that in vision transformers, columns of the attention matrix contribute unequally to the final computation, and this imbalance grows with network depth. Based on this, the authors add an input-dependent bias to the query-key dot product, giving each token a scalar score of its expected influence during attention. This score serves as a proxy for pruning attention maps. Across several transformer model sizes, the method substantially reduces attention computation in FLOPs and inference latency while keeping most of the original classification accuracy.

entry.title: BhopalMLS: A LiDAR Dataset for Understanding Scenes in Mixed Urban Areas
entry.summary: BhopalMLS: A LiDAR Dataset for Semantic Scene Understanding in Heterogeneous Urban Environments arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces BhopalMLS, a large mobile laser scanning dataset collected in Bhopal, India, covering about 10 km of roads with over 1.2 billion points and 19,518 annotated instances. It provides 62 fine-grained static categories organized into 12-class and 21-class benchmark taxonomies. Fine-tuned foundation models outperform supervised baselines on segmentation, and cross-dataset experiments show that models trained on BhopalMLS transfer better than the reverse.

entry.title: Therapy-FIS: A Dataset for Automatically Assessing Therapists' Interpersonal Skills in Psychotherapy
entry.summary: Therapy-FIS: A Dataset for Assessing Facilitative Interpersonal Skills in Psychotherapeutic Setting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces Therapy-FIS, a dataset for automatically assessing facilitative interpersonal skills (FIS) of mental health professionals during standardized psychotherapy tasks. It contains facial, acoustic, and textual signals from 890 therapist videos responding to 8 mock patient videos, rated on eight FIS subscales and an overall score. The authors establish a benchmark with two downstream rating tasks and propose a baseline model, DyadicFIS, which achieves the best macro CCC scores of 0.2807 and 0.3299 on those tasks.

entry.title: A SAT encoding for ladder-shaped at-most-K cardinality constraints
entry.summary: SAT Encoding for Set of At-Most-K Cardinality Constraints with Ladder Shape arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a new SAT encoding for a sequence of At-Most-K cardinality constraints arranged in a ladder shape, called Ladder AMK constraints. The method splits the sequence into blocks, encodes each block as a whole using Sequential Counter, and adds clauses linking adjacent blocks. The authors report fewer variables and clauses than prior BDD-based encodings, and faster solving on tests including the Anti-bandwidth and Nurse Rostering problems.

entry.title: ReXMo: End-to-end video character replacement that keeps expressions and motion
entry.summary: ReXMo: End-to-End Video Character Replacement with Expression and Motion Preservation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents ReXMo, a framework that replaces actors in videos while preserving their facial expressions, motions, and scene dynamics. It supports single-, multi-, and selective character replacement and is trained on paired synthetic videos that share the same performance but different identities. The authors report that ReXMo outperforms existing methods in identity fidelity, motion consistency, expression preservation, and visual quality.

entry.title: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning: a method that uses a frozen model copy given privileged information, such as answers, to guide token weighting in supervised fine-tuning
entry.summary: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper analyzes token-level weighting schemes in supervised fine-tuning, finding that dynamic weighting such as DFT induces a heavily sharpened target distribution, while static weighting fits a distribution proportional to the data distribution times a frozen prior. Based on this, it proposes Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning (SPFT), which uses a frozen copy of the initial model conditioned on privileged information, such as ground-truth answers, as the prior for token weighting. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation show SPFT outperforms standard SFT and other baselines.

entry.title: Testing whether AI language models can judge the quality of replies to online hate speech
entry.summary: Evaluating LLMs as Judges of Counterspeech Quality Against Online Hate Speech arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether large language models can assess the quality of counterspeech, responses that counter online hate speech, in place of human experts. The authors test 12 open-weight models on relevance, coherence, aggressiveness, and suitableness using several prompting methods. Agreement with human experts is low, with the best configuration reaching a linear-weighted Cohen's κ of 0.19 and Spearman's ρ of 0.42 on coherence. The models also agree with each other more than they agree with the experts.

entry.title: MambaHand: Learning Hand Gesture Identity and Motion Patterns with Mamba for Authentication
entry.summary: MambaHand: Local Identity and Behavioral Sequence Learning with Mamba for Dynamic Hand Gesture Authentication arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes MambaHand Net, a two-stream framework that combines CNNs with Mamba for dynamic hand gesture authentication. A local identity stream captures frame-level fine-grained cues, while a behavioral sequence stream uses bidirectional Mamba to model long-range motion dependencies. The two streams are fused into a discriminative identity representation, and the method achieves state-of-the-art average performance on the SCUT-DHGA benchmark.

entry.title: QueryFlow: Multi-Hop Graph Retrieval with Adaptive Query Evolution
entry.summary: QueryFlow: Multi-Hop Graph Retrieval with Adaptive Query Evolution arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes QueryFlow, a method for retrieving evidence across multiple related pages for multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation. It recurrently merges query-conditioned summaries of graph context into a shared query state that guides subsequent relation propagation. On four multi-hop question answering datasets, it improves macro Recall@10, Full Recall@10, and LLM-Acc by 4.98, 8.40, and 8.0 percentage points over representative baselines.

entry.title: Polyp Matching With Deep Learning: Checking Whether Multiple Images Show the Same Polyp
entry.summary: Polyp Matching Using Deep Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study presents a contrastive learning approach using a Siamese neural network to determine whether multiple colon capsule endoscopy images depict the same polyp, aiming to avoid over-counting. The model was trained on a Danish CareForColon2015 trial dataset containing 5,103 same-polyp image pairs and 5,103 different-polyp pairs, using several backbone networks and a cosine distance metric. Experiments reported classification accuracy of up to 92% and AUC values close to 0.98.

entry.title: Gradient-guided orientation learning for weakly supervised rotated object detection
entry.summary: Gradient-Guided Orientation Learning for Weakly Supervised Oriented Object Detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses weakly supervised oriented object detection, which detects rotated objects using cheaper annotations such as horizontal boxes or points. The authors extract dominant gradient-based orientation cues from object regions and convert them into pseudo-angle labels for auxiliary supervision, requiring no rotated box annotations or extra learnable parameters. They also propose an orientation-aware evaluation metric that adds angular discrepancies to standard AP, and report experiments showing improved detection and orientation estimation.

entry.title: Policy Network Diffusion: Using Diffusion Models to Generate Reinforcement Learning Policy Parameters
entry.summary: Policy Network Diffusion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether diffusion models can generate the parameters of policy networks in reinforcement learning and whether the resulting policies generalize. The authors propose DPPG, which combines a Transformer-based autoencoder that compresses network parameters into patches with a task-conditioned diffusion model. Experiments report that a single DPPG model synthesizes high-quality policies across Classic Control, Atari, and MuJoCo tasks, and converges faster with competitive performance in previously unseen environments.

entry.title: CAPSkip: A Training Method That Skips Backpropagation for Some Correctly Classified Examples
entry.summary: CAPSkip: Cancellation-Aware Prefix Skipping for Selective Backpropagation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes CAPSkip, a selective backpropagation method that forwards all examples in a mini-batch but back-propagates only some of them. Among correctly classified examples, it skips the longest prefix, ordered by last-layer gradient norm, whose summed gradient stays within a relative budget of the full batch gradient. In fine-tuning DeiT-S on CIFAR-100, the method ran 103 epochs in 0.576 times the time of dense training and outperformed an approximately time-matched 59-epoch dense run.

entry.title: 3D coronary artery reconstruction from few views using a diffusion prior
entry.summary: Sparse-View 3D Coronary Reconstruction from Vessel Segmentations Using a Diffusion Prior arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a method to reconstruct 3D coronary artery anatomy from a small number of angiographic views. It combines a 3D diffusion prior trained on coronary vessel masks, visual-hull initialization, and projection-based data consistency. Tested on simulated angiograms from ImageCAS CT angiography volumes with two, four, and eight views, the method achieved higher mean Dice and clDice than visual hull, DIP, and hash-grid INR baselines under reduced contrast across 50 cases.

entry.title: SCANO: A neural operator that keeps boundary conditions intact when training on sampled 3D thermal meshes
entry.summary: SCANO: Restoring Boundary-Condition Completeness in Sampled Meshes with a Sliced-Cross-Attention Neural Operator for 3D Thermal Fields arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper addresses the problem that training neural operators on subsampled million-cell meshes can distort boundary information and hurt accuracy. It identifies three distortion mechanisms and derives four consistency conditions that can be checked before training. The authors propose two modules, Boundary Quadrature Attention and Anchored Global State, which are added to a scalable backbone to form SCANO. Evaluations on benchmarks and a data-centre thermal dataset show lower whole-mesh error, regional predictions aligned with whole-mesh ones, and room-scale field prediction in under one second.

entry.title: Estimating realized skewness with a convolutional neural network
entry.summary: Estimating "Realized" Skewness using Convolutional Neural Network arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a new estimator of monthly skewness that uses 5-minute high-frequency data through a mapping of convolutional neural network layers followed by multilayer perceptrons. Monte Carlo experiments with stochastic volatility models, with and without jumps, show it reduces finite-sample bias compared with existing realized-skewness estimators and stays accurate under model misspecification. Empirically, the estimator shows temporal stability and performs cross-sectionally in skewness-sorted portfolios.

entry.title: SparseGraph-I2P: Consistency-Guided Selection for Efficient Image-to-Point-Cloud Alignment
entry.summary: SparseGraph-I2P: Consistency-Guided Hypothesis Selection for Efficient Image-to-Point-Cloud Registration arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes SparseGraph-I2P, a method for aligning images with point clouds using a coarse-to-fine approach. A coarse hypothesis graph uses appearance and depth cues to select a fixed set of patch pairs, while sparse fine matching avoids redundant pixel-point comparisons. With sensor depth, it filters correspondences for a single EPnP solve and achieves the highest recall and lowest latency on RGB-D Scenes V2 and 7-Scenes.

entry.title: Can Science Networks Work Without Pluralist Agents? A simulation study of whether communities holding rival theories shape how collective belief changes.
entry.summary: Can Network Models of Science Do Without Pluralist Agents? arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper asks why science keeps working even though its models are repeatedly shown to be wrong. It builds a theoretical and experimental model comparing communities of pluralist agents, which can hold rival theories at once, with monist agents that keep only a single model. Using a multi-agent variational inference setting, the experiments show how communities with rival theories move through uncertain periods and shift which theories they accept, and how communicated information affects beliefs.

entry.title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings
entry.summary: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces relative rank models, a probabilistic framework for ranking distributions based on structured coarsenings of the ranking space. The framework relaxes the mutual exclusivity constraints of rankings while preserving relative order information. It gives conditional independence a well-defined meaning for rankings, so they can be modeled with Bayesian networks and standard learning and inference methods. Two prominent ranking models based on independence assumptions are shown to be special cases.

entry.title: Multi-path Mamba diffusion method for filling in and labeling 3D point cloud scenes
entry.summary: Multi-Path Mamba Diffusion for 3D Point Cloud Semantic Scene Completion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces MPath Mamba, a diffusion network that fills in missing geometry and predicts semantic labels in 3D point cloud scene data. It combines state space modeling with diffusion-based generation and operates in the conditioned latent space of a variational autoencoder. Experiments on the SemanticKITTI benchmark show the approach achieves highly competitive results for 3D point cloud semantic scene completion.

entry.title: ValQID: Learning the Net Value of Semantic Query Groups for Web Device Identification
entry.summary: ValQID: Learning the Net Value of Semantic Query Groups for Web Device Identification arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents ValQID, a method for identifying the vendors and types of devices behind Web interfaces, a step important for asset inventory and security management. It uses a relation graph to combine device identity cues scattered across page text, configuration fields, and management functions, and evaluates semantic questions efficiently with DSEJEV. Based on the current identification state, it adaptively allocates computation. On real Web response data, it achieves gains of up to 47.1% in joint macro-F1 and up to 82.1% in macro-F1 for low-frequency vendors over a state-of-the-art method, and DSEJEV is up to 8.58 times faster than general-purpose language models.

entry.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing Dataset in Ground Effect for Testing AI Aerodynamic Models
entry.summary: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper releases a CFD dataset of a 3D wing operating near the ground, built from 770 RANS simulations of 194 wing configurations typical of motorsport. Six neural network architectures are tested on predicting surface pressure and wall shear stress, from which drag and lift coefficients are derived. The dataset is intended as a challenging benchmark for surrogate CFD models.

entry.title: A model of power engineering research that learns its dynamics and simulates what-if scenarios
entry.summary: A research world model of power engineering learns its dynamics and reveals what-ifs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces research world models, which treat a research field as a dynamical system that can be acted upon, and builds one for power engineering from 1.1 million papers. A language model converts each paper into role-typed concepts, graph-temporal neural networks learn how the concept network evolves, and operators estimate intervention effects from natural experiments in the publication record. In temporally held-out tests, the model forecast which concepts would grow and which method-target pairs would first be joined, and its estimated intervention effects matched those realized in natural experiments it had not seen.

entry.title: Curriculum unlearning: how simple-to-complex teaching helps humans and neural networks
entry.summary: Curriculum unlearning in humans and neural networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper investigates why curricula that teach simple rules before exceptions are effective. Using a canonical behavioural task and neural network modelling, the authors show that both humans and neural networks exhibit a simplicity bias, learning simple rules that underfit the data. In neural networks, this bias is accompanied by compression of neural representations. Simple-to-complex curricula help both learner types overcome this compression and develop representations suited to the task. The authors also confirm that learners pre-exposed to simple tasks, with more compressed initial representations, benefit more from curricula.

entry.title: Inter-Agent Influence: Testing How AI Agents Persuade, Deceive, and Coerce Each Other
entry.summary: Inter-Agent Influence: Evaluating Persuasion, Deception, and Coercion in Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether AI agents in multi-agent systems can steer each other's behaviour through persuasion, deception, or coercion. The authors test three such capabilities across five realistic evaluation environments using agents built on frontier language models. In oversight environments, all tested models shifted an overseer's decision from rejection to approval using these methods. The study also found successful influence in peer-to-peer settings, where an agent redirected a peer's safety research trajectory.

entry.title: SEEK-VAU: Video Anomaly Understanding through Active, Verifiable Evidence Search
entry.summary: SEEK-VAU: Towards Evidence-Faithful Video Anomaly Understanding via Agentic Search arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper notes that current video anomaly understanding systems reason over evidence gathered in a fixed feed-forward way and cannot search for missing evidence once reasoning begins. It proposes SEEK-VAU, which frames the task as a bounded agentic search-and-verify process that collects evidence across the precursor, trigger, and aftermath stages of an anomaly event chain and checks sufficiency before finalizing. The authors also introduce evidence-faithful counterfactual verification (EFCV) as a reward for supportive, compact, and necessary evidence, and SEEK-Bench, a benchmark with temporal interval annotations, semantic QA, and event-chain stage labels.

entry.title: Predicting Empty Space in Forest Canopies from Drone Imaging
entry.summary: Predicting Void Points in Self-Occluding Forest Volumes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This thesis addresses overestimation of forest biomass in drone-based synthetic aperture imaging, where occluded regions appear occupied. Instead of changing the imaging process, it modifies training labels by rendering depth-clipped slabs that explicitly mark void space as a negative class. On a held-out scene, an RGB-input volumetric network achieved the highest IoU of 0.6514, outperforming COLMAP and DepthAnything3.

entry.title: Can LLM Assistants Handle Regulatory Work? Results of the 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge
entry.summary: Are LLM Assistants Regulatory Ready? Answers from regenold's 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces a benchmark of 110 expert-written open-ended questions about the EU AI Act, each with an exemplary answer, correctness criteria, and expected references. It evaluates large language model assistants on answer correctness, reference quality, conciseness, tone, and latency, including a multi-turn mode that simulates user pushback. In the 2026 challenge based on this benchmark, three off-the-shelf baselines and five purpose-built assistants were tested, and only two of the five consistently outperformed the baselines, with one scoring highly on all metrics. The results indicate that specialized development alone does not guarantee better performance, underscoring the importance of evaluating assistants used in regulatory affairs.

entry.title: CANDO: A residual reinforcement learning method that adjusts robot policy noise and actions conservatively
entry.summary: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes CANDO, a residual reinforcement learning method that improves a frozen pretrained generative robot policy in both noise space and action space. It builds on CNDO, which learns state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latent samples and regulates adaptation with conservative value estimation and gated execution, then adds a local action-space correction. The authors report 76.1 NAUC and a 91.4% final success rate, exceeding the best single-space results by 6.6 NAUC and 4.1 percentage points.

entry.title: BtsPruner: A Role-Aware Method for Pruning Visual Tokens in Large Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: BtsPruner: Role-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Large Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Large vision-language models process many visual tokens, which makes inference costly in computation and memory. This paper proposes BtsPruner, a training-free pruning framework that keeps complementary visual tokens under a fixed budget by accounting for the different roles tokens play during encoding. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, it retains 91.6% of the dense model's performance using only 32 of 576 visual tokens. On the high-resolution LLaVA-NeXT-7B, it achieves up to a 5.95x CUDA-latency speedup.

entry.title: The Price of List Replicability: Tight Bounds for Bias Estimation
entry.summary: The Price of List Replicability: Tight Bounds for Bias Estimation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the sample complexity of list replicable algorithms that estimate the biases of d coins. It gives the first nontrivial sample complexity lower bound for this problem and an improved algorithm that matches it up to polylogarithmic factors. For list size d+1 the optimal sample complexity is Õ(d²/ε²), and for list sizes k between d+1 and 2^d the upper and lower bounds both equal Õ(d²/(ε² log k)).

entry.title: Learning to Falsify: Hierarchical Multiple Instance Learning for Detecting AI-Generated Images
entry.summary: Learning to Falsify: Hierarchical Multiple Instance Learning for High Resolution AI-Generated Image Detection arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of reliably detecting increasingly photorealistic AI-generated images, especially high-resolution ones. It frames detection as a falsification-driven multiple instance learning problem, where one fake patch falsifies the whole image while a real image requires all patches to be authentic. The authors propose LTF, a hierarchical multiple instance learning framework with Cross-Shuffle training, and FATAS, a plug-and-play test-time aggregation module that improves existing detectors without retraining.

entry.title: E2I-Flow: EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Wavelet-Temporal Cross-Attention and Conditional Flow Matching
entry.summary: E2I-Flow: EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Wavelet-Temporal Cross-Attention and Conditional Flow Matching arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes E2I-Flow, a framework that decodes visual information from non-invasive EEG brain signals and reconstructs images. It uses an EEG encoder combining a stationary-wavelet frequency branch and a temporal-mixing branch, fused through bidirectional cross-attention, and aligns the resulting representations to image embeddings. A Transformer-based conditional flow-matching model then predicts visual embeddings from the aligned EEG representation for image synthesis. The authors report strong zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval and better reconstruction than several state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: Lessons and pitfalls from using AI to assist large-scale A/B testing
entry.summary: Learnings and Pitfalls from AI-Assisted A/B Experimentation at Scale arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper shares lessons from building and operating an AI agent that assists with A/B experiments. The authors argue that trust is preserved by bounding where a language model's nondeterminism can reach: the model selects and sequences procedures, while deterministic code computes every reported quantity. The paper also reports three surprising findings, including that withholding information from the model improved its answers.

entry.title: Variational learning using exponential families defined on Lie groups
entry.summary: Variational Learning with Lie Group Exponential Families arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper extends a previously proposed Lie group framework for variational Bayesian learning to any general Lie group. It shows that linear approximations of the Lie group algorithm generalize the Bayesian learning rule (BLR). The key tool is the harmonic exponential family, a class of Lie group exponential families tied to representations of Lie groups, which provides a systematic way to build efficiently implementable variational learning algorithms.

entry.title: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models
entry.summary: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents the first systematic bias and fairness audit of a typed decision model (\jev{}) designed for recruitment. It examines how explicit demographic attributes and implicit candidate cues affect screening scores, rankings, and shortlisting, comparing these effects against a noise baseline from name substitutions and typographical variations. The study also assesses output validity, latency, and cost. Counterfactual CV datasets and evaluation code are released for reproducibility.

entry.title: Signals: continuous diagnostics for AI agents that find and fix faulty behavior
entry.summary: Signals: Continuous Diagnostics of AI Agents arXiv · Nov 3, 2026AI agents can make wrong decisions or waste resources even when their tools and infrastructure work normally, and their nondeterministic behavior makes such problems hard to reproduce. This paper presents Signals, a method that identifies these problems from agent execution traces and suggests concrete remediations, built on a taxonomy of 45 problem types in eight families. On public agent executions, it reached 91.43% F1 when matching Signals to reference issues, about 18 percentage points above a one-pass LLM control using the same model and taxonomy.

entry.title: AttriSwarm: Agent Swarm Framework for Tracing Answers Across Document Pages
entry.summary: AttriSwarm: Orchestrating Agent Swarms for Cross-Page Visual Attribution arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes AttriSwarm, a multi-agent swarm framework that identifies which document pages support an answer and localizes the specific evidence regions on them. A leader agent handles global reasoning across pages, while subagents attribute evidence page by page in parallel. The authors also build AttriDoc, a cross-page QA dataset linking supporting pages to annotated evidence regions, and use it to train each role, reporting average gains over the training-free version of 18.94, 29.34, and 23.04 points in answer accuracy, page-level F1, and region-level IoU.

entry.title: Per-sample approximate unlearning with provable error bounds
entry.summary: Sample-Grained Approximate Unlearning with Provable Per-Sample Bounds arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies approximate machine unlearning, which removes the influence of a designated forget set from a trained model without full retraining. The authors introduce SALA, a plug-in optimization framework that steers each individual sample toward its correct target distribution. They also propose a sample-grained distribution gap metric and provide theoretical guarantees that SALA bounds per-sample discrepancy from retraining. Experiments on classification and generation tasks report gap reductions of up to 86.67%.

entry.title: Spatial Memory for AR Glasses: Recalling Past Scenes Through Selective Visual Capture
entry.summary: Spatial Memory for AR Glasses: Hierarchical Visual Acquisition and Source-Linked Recall arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a spatial-memory system that lets optical see-through AR glasses recall earlier physical encounters. A dual-camera prototype uses hierarchical visual acquisition, source-linked storage, and staged retrieval to answer questions about past scenes. In a 131.35-second egocentric replay, the system selected six RGB views from 648 monitoring observations and ran feature extraction on 97.7% of them. The results show selective RGB capture, while frequent local inference remains a cost.

entry.title: Hybrid particle-voxel dynamics for multimodal 3D world simulation
entry.summary: Hybrid Particle-Voxel Dynamics for Multimodal 3D World Simulation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents 3D World Simulator, an action-conditioned world model that jointly predicts appearance, geometry, and tactile observations from a unified 3D representation. It combines a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder, which compresses point clouds into compact 3D voxel latents, with a latent dynamics model conditioned on actions. The authors report interactive, long-horizon multimodal prediction at 50 Hz, and show uses in generating data for policy training and evaluation and in model-based planning with unseen objects and robot configurations.

entry.title: SPA-Q: A structure-preserving quantization method that shrinks monocular depth estimation models
entry.summary: SPA-Q: Structure-Preserving Adaptive Post-Training Quantization for Monocular Depth Estimation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Monocular depth estimation models like Depth Anything are strong but costly to run. This paper proposes SPA-Q, a post-training quantization framework that compresses such models while keeping their attention patterns and feature distributions intact. It reports better results than existing post-training quantization methods at 4-bit precision on the NYUv2 and KITTI datasets.

entry.title: Few-shot radar target recognition using polarimetric scattering-structure contrastive learning
entry.summary: Polarimetric Scattering-Structure Contrastive Learning for Few-Shot HRRP Recognition arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses few-shot high-resolution range profile (HRRP) recognition, where targets vary strongly with aspect angle and novel classes have sparse support samples. The proposed PSS-CL method represents dominant local responses by their affinities to canonical polarimetric scattering mechanisms, normalized range locations, and energy contributions, and transfers this structure to the HRRP encoder through a symmetric cross-view objective. On a six-class measured dataset, PSS-CL reaches 81.73%, 86.92%, and 90.98% mean class accuracy in cross-aspect 1-, 3-, and 5-shot recognition, outperforming the best competing results by 5.62%, 3.09%, and 3.56%.

entry.title: CDIM: Cross-Modal Information Maximization for Online Test-Time Adaptation of CLIP and DINO
entry.summary: Bridging CLIP with DINO: Cross-Modal Information Maximization for Online Test-Time Adaptation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper identifies modality bias, where CLIP's visual encoder under image corruptions confidently maps distorted features to wrong text classes. The proposed CDIM method combines the frozen self-supervised DINO v2 backbone with CLIP via a cross-covariance logit ensemble, and adds a gated information-maximization objective and online logit adjustment for online test-time adaptation. The authors report that it outperforms compared CLIP-based online TTA baselines on ImageNet-C, CIFAR10-C, and CIFAR100-C.

entry.title: Diagnosing faults by reconstructing unmeasured variables with Gödel-regularized virtual sensors
entry.summary: Reconstruction-Based Diagnosis through Gödel-Regularized Virtual Observability arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Many components in technical systems cannot be fitted with sensors, so existing sensors often detect a fault only after its effects have spread, making isolation difficult. The paper introduces virtual sensors, where external knowledge identifies fault-sensitive variables for each component and fault type, and a neural observer trained only on normal data reconstructs missing variables to predict normal behavior. Deviations are turned into local symptoms and compared by onset time to identify root causes. Gödel logic encodes physical knowledge and guides training, and the approach is evaluated on synthetic networks, the Tennessee Eastman Process, and two modular production plant datasets.

entry.title: CogniLife: Continuous Cognitive Distillation for Multi-Expert AI Agent Marketplaces
entry.summary: CogniLife: Continuous Cognitive Distillation for Deployed Multi-Expert Agent Marketplaces arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes CogniLife, a framework that turns attributed creator observations into revisable decision rules and domain procedures for multi-expert AI agent marketplaces. Its Creator Profiles and Expert Journals design is described as not yet implemented, while a deployed platform partially realizes the surrounding lifecycle. On the 85-task offline benchmark ProfyBench-v1, the full configuration scored 4.65/5 against 4.01 for Raw LLM and 4.28 for Expert Prompt. The authors note these scores do not test cold-expert mitigation, cross-expert transfer, or longitudinal distillation.

entry.title: TEMPO: a method that lets language models read time-series signals via discrete tokens
entry.summary: TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents TEMPO, which adds discrete codes from a context-aware Transformer tokenizer to a language model's vocabulary so that numerical signals and text can be processed together. Using a Qwen3-4B backbone with task-specific fine-tuning, it reports macro-F1 scores of 89.0% for activity recognition, 85.0% for sleep staging, and 86.0% for bearing-fault diagnosis. The authors also present time-series question answering and qualitative bearing-diagnosis examples.

entry.title: Self-improving lab automation that revises its own hardware and software toward a goal
entry.summary: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a research approach in which agents revise hardware, software, models and protocols using physical measurements to reach a scientific goal. The concept is tested in an optical color-matching study using an iPad, smart glasses and a spectroradiometer. Spectral feedback reduced one target color difference from 19.756 to 1.211 ΔE76*, and all five targets improved in a separate comparison.

entry.title: ReListen: Training-free method letting a frozen audio model find evidence in hour-long recordings
entry.summary: ReListen: Training-Free Evidence Localization in Hour-Long Audio with Frozen Audio Language Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes ReListen, a method in which a frozen audio language model scans 20-second windows of a long recording and scores how likely each one helps answer the question, then answers from the highest-scoring minute. On VoiceGiraffe questions, this minute overlaps the annotated evidence 88.5% of the time, more often than transcript retrieval. The authors report it exceeds a transcript of the whole recording by 9.2 points on VoiceGiraffe and answers faster than transcript-based systems.

entry.title: A Parametric Linear Conic Projection Method for Structured Sparse Attention
entry.summary: A Parametric Linear Conic Projection for Structured Sparse Attention arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces the Cone Alignment Index (CAI), a scale-invariant sparsity measure tied to Lorentz-cone geometry, and analyzes its probabilistic distribution. Two projections are derived from it and shown to yield the same sparsity threshold and active support. A bilevel framework then generates hardware-friendly structured masks, including row-wise, column-wise, and diagonal patterns, aimed at accelerating Transformer attention.

entry.title: KeyWise: A Lightweight Per-Key Architecture for Video-Only Piano Transcription
entry.summary: KeyWise: Efficient Video-Only Piano Transcription with a Lightweight Per-Key Architecture arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents KeyWise, a lightweight method that transcribes piano performances from top-view video alone, avoiding audio problems such as sustain-pedal effects and noisy soundtracks. The keyboard is divided into 88 regions, and one small recurrent network shared across all keys tracks each key over time. On PianoVAM, KeyWise matches the onset accuracy of the state-of-the-art V2N with about 1.3M parameters instead of 28.2M and runs 4.7 times faster. On PianoYT, a model pre-trained on PianoVAM reaches 69.4% onset F1 at 100 ms, but it needs fine-tuning for new recording conditions.

entry.title: Hierarchical evolutionary optimization for UAV-assisted NOMA-MEC networks
entry.summary: Hierarchical Intelligent Evolutionary Optimization for UAV-Assisted NOMA-MEC Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how multiple UAVs can jointly manage trajectories, task offloading and communication and computing resources in a network combining mobile edge computing and NOMA, with tasks of different priorities. The authors propose HIEA, a hierarchical algorithm that uses multi-head deep Q-networks for decisions, a channel-quality-guided population initialization, adaptive evolutionary search and successive convex approximation refinement. Simulations report gains over benchmark schemes of up to 6.5% in throughput, 13.6% in task completion rate and 15.3% in energy efficiency.

entry.title: Fixing the Symptom but Missing the Cause: A Study of Scientific Reasoning Failure
entry.summary: Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause: Anatomy of a Scientific Reasoning Failure arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper tests large language model agents in controlled synthetic regulatory systems, where they must experimentally find a hidden fault and rescue an abnormal phenotype. Across seven models, every one restored healthy phenotypes more often than it correctly identified the fault. Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 rescued every organism but diagnosed only 55% and 35% correctly. The authors find that agents often encountered evidence distinguishing the competing causes yet still misdiagnosed the system.

entry.title: Explicit visual grounding of objects for video reasoning segmentation
entry.summary: Beyond Token Representations: Explicit Visual Object Grounding for Video Reasoning Segmentation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses video reasoning segmentation, which finds and segments objects in videos based on reasoning queries. It argues that existing segmentation tokens are semantically monotonous and spatially ambiguous, so it generates explicit bounding boxes and point sets via a multimodal large language model refined through multi-step dialogue. It also adds diversified auxiliary queries with cross-query consistency and a prompt-based keyframe selection strategy. Experiments on eight datasets show significant gains over state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: A GeoAI and machine learning method for consistent high-resolution land cover maps from time-series NAIP imagery
entry.summary: Using GeoAI and machine learning tools for consistent high-resolution land cover mapping based on time-series NAIP imagery arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a dual-track workflow that produces temporally consistent 1-meter land cover maps from NAIP aerial imagery without historical training samples. Higher-quality 2009–2017 imagery is classified with a pretrained U-Net/ResNet-34 model and refined using the Segment Anything Model, while lower-quality 2004–2008 imagery is reconstructed through an NLCD-based spatiotemporal bridging and label back-casting pipeline. Evaluated across six counties in North Carolina and Pennsylvania, the maps achieved overall accuracies of 0.887 (2014), 0.886 (2017), and 0.733 (2004).

entry.title: Is Forgetting Unified? Concept Unlearning Across Image Generation and Understanding
entry.summary: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies whether a unified multimodal model can forget a target concept in both image generation and visual understanding at once. The authors introduce UUBench, a diagnostic benchmark with 30 target concepts and 60 semantically related neighboring concepts. They find that existing single-pathway methods achieve limited joint forgetting, and propose UniForget, which reaches joint forgetting rates of 80.0% on BAGEL-7B-MoT and 92.7% on Janus-Pro-7B.

entry.title: From Watching to Steering: Human-Agent Collaboration via Execution Traces
entry.summary: From Watching to Steering: Enabling Human-Coding Agent Collaboration through Execution Traces arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents Vibetrace, an interactive system built on OpenCode for visualizing and intervening in the execution of coding agents. Users can inspect agent actions and failures through interactive execution traces, fork execution from prior steps to apply targeted corrections, and distill traces and feedback into reusable skills. On SWE-bench Verified, the distilled skills reduced input tokens by 23.0% and cost by 15.5%, while raising pass rate from 65.0% to 68.0%. User studies report improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional log-based interaction.

entry.title: A theoretical study of the Muon optimizer for training Transformers to predict the next token
entry.summary: Theoretical Analysis of Muon on Transformers for Next-Token Prediction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper analyzes how the Muon optimizer trains Transformers for next-token prediction, a core task in language models. Training is split into two phases: a preprocessing phase that learns the output-value component and a main phase that learns the key-query component. The authors derive convergence results for both phases and argue that Muon's update rule helps models learn which tokens matter for prediction. Experiments on next-token prediction tasks support the theoretical findings.

entry.title: SaMA: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method using expanded Kronecker products
entry.summary: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes SaMA (Scalable Morpho Adaptation), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large models. It relaxes the shared-block constraint in the Kronecker product factorization, letting its effective rank grow quadratically with the parameter budget, up to full rank. The authors show its invariance manifold collapses to a diagonal group, which makes it more friendly to adaptive optimizers. On commonsense and arithmetic reasoning benchmarks, SaMA outperforms strong PEFT baselines while using fewer parameters.

entry.title: τ-Rec-Books: A Disclosure-Controlled Benchmark for Eliciting Requirements in Agentic Recommenders
entry.summary: τ-Rec-Books: A Disclosure-Controlled Benchmark for Requirement Elicitation in Agentic Recommender Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces τ-Rec-Books, a benchmark for testing how well AI agents draw out a user's needs during conversational book recommendation. Requirements are revealed at the start, partly on request, or never, and hidden ones must be inferred from accept or reject feedback. Across 450 tasks built on a 20,000-book Wikidata catalog, agent success rates drop sharply as more requirements stay hidden.

entry.title: AI-assisted adaptive search method for scheduling agile Earth observation satellites
entry.summary: Large Language Model-Assisted Adaptive Heuristic Search for Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses how agile Earth observation satellites should schedule imaging tasks within limited observation windows while handling attitude maneuvers and energy limits. The proposed method uses a large language model to generate an initial task-selection heuristic and then refine it during ant colony search based on search results. Across six scenarios with 50 to 200 imaging tasks, the method achieved 4.3% to 9.6% higher mean observation benefit than the strongest baseline.

entry.title: DynOSeg: Separating Moving Objects in Video Using Motion and Geometry Fusion
entry.summary: DynOSeg: Dynamic Object Segmentation via Motion-Geometry Fusion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces DynOSeg, a method for separating moving objects from the static background in videos. It uses a two-stage fusion approach, first combining a geometry-aware residual map with depth encoding to represent camera and object motion, then adding semantic features to refine object understanding. The authors also present CARLA-MOS, a new synthetic urban-driving dataset for training. Experiments show DynOSeg consistently outperforms published state-of-the-art methods across a range of datasets.

entry.title: A Bayesian-geometric reinterpretation of classical optimal design criteria
entry.summary: A Bayesian-Geometric Reading of Classical Model-Based Optimal Design arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Classical model-based optimal design criteria (D, T, L, C, and A optimality) are usually derived from the Cramér-Rao bound by optimizing scalar functions of the Fisher information matrix. This paper gives a complementary view in which, as the sample size grows, each criterion appears as the leading term of an expected dissimilarity between prior and posterior, with the Fisher information entering via the Bernstein-von Mises limit. The five criteria are presented as instances of a common Bayesian-geometric template determined by the choice of dissimilarity, prior parametrization, and approximation scheme. E-optimality is obtained as a min-max robustification of C-optimality.

entry.title: Near-zero token embeddings quietly stall training in gated sequence models
entry.summary: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper surveys 291 open-weight language model repositories and finds that 52.6% of untied gated and hybrid checkpoints contain input embeddings with norms below 10^-6, compared with 0% of weight-tied models. In gated sequence models, such near-zero tokens can amplify gradients enormously, and gradient clipping can overflow and zero out a batch's gradients. The authors propose GroupClip for released checkpoints and GateFloor for pretraining.
